3: // Generates dev-only wrangler.dev.jsonc files for dynamic service bindings,
4: // then launches `wrangler dev` with all discovered workers.
5: //
6: // Flags:
7: //   --use-workers-ai-binding   Include the Workers AI binding in
8: //                               workshop-backend (requires Cloudflare login).
9: //   --port PORT                 Listen on PORT instead of 8787. Overrides VITE_BACKEND_HOST.
10: //
11: // Env:
12: //   VITE_BACKEND_HOST=localhost:9000  Also pass --port 9000 to wrangler dev.
13: 
14: import {
15:   existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, readdirSync, statSync,
16: } from "node:fs";
17: import { spawn, type ChildProcess } from "node:child_process";
18: import { connect } from "node:net";
19: import { constants } from "node:os";
20: import { join, dirname } from "node:path";
21: import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
22: import { parse } from "jsonc-parser";
23: import { resolveBinEntry } from "./bin-entry.ts";
24: import { getDevServerConfig } from "./dev-server-config.ts";
25: import { killProcessTree } from "./kill-process-tree.ts";
26: import { pnpmCommand } from "./pnpm-command.ts";
27: import type { ServiceBinding, WranglerBuild } from "./release/manifest-lib.ts";
28: 
29: const SCRIPTS_DIR = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
30: const ROOT = join(SCRIPTS_DIR, "..");
31: const PACKAGES_DIR = join(ROOT, "packages");
32: const WORKSHOP_BACKEND_DIR = join(PACKAGES_DIR, "workshop-backend");
33: 
34: /** A gatekeeper package as {@link findGatekeepers} discovers it. */
35: interface Gatekeeper {
36:   /** Package directory name, which is also the worker name. */
37:   name: string;
38:   /** Absolute path to the package directory. */
39:   dir: string;
40: }
41: 
42: // Load a root `.dev.vars` file (KEY=VALUE lines) into process.env for local development. Existing
43: // shell environment values take precedence. This file is gitignored and may hold local secrets.
44: function loadDevVars(): void {
45:   const path = join(ROOT, ".dev.vars");
46:   if (!existsSync(path)) return;
47:   for (const rawLine of readFileSync(path, "utf8").split("\n")) {
48:     const line = rawLine.trim();
49:     if (!line || line.startsWith("#")) continue;
50:     const eq = line.indexOf("=");
51:     if (eq === -1) continue;
52:     const key = line.slice(0, eq).trim();
53:     let value = line.slice(eq + 1).trim();
54:     // Strip surrounding single or double quotes.
55:     if ((value.startsWith('"') && value.endsWith('"')) ||
56:         (value.startsWith("'") && value.endsWith("'"))) {
57:       value = value.slice(1, -1);
58:     }
59:     if (process.env[key] === undefined) process.env[key] = value;
60:   }
61: }
62: loadDevVars();
63: 
64: const useWorkersAi = process.argv.includes("--use-workers-ai-binding");
65: 
66: // In `run-local` mode the backend serves the pre-built frontend bundle as static assets (there is no
67: // Vite dev server). In normal dev mode we leave assets unconfigured so the frontend is served by
68: // Vite on :3000 and no `vite build` is required to start the dev server.
69: const serveFrontendAssets = process.argv.includes("--serve-frontend-assets");
70: 
71: let backendHost: string;
72: let wranglerPort: string | null;
73: try {
74:   ({ backendHost, wranglerPort } = getDevServerConfig(
75:       process.argv.slice(2), process.env.VITE_BACKEND_HOST));
76: } catch (err) {
77:   console.error((err as Error).message);
78:   process.exit(1);
79: }

81: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
82: // Discover gatekeeper packages.
83: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
84: function findGatekeepers(parentDir: string): Gatekeeper[] {
85:   try {
86:     return readdirSync(parentDir)
87:         .filter(name => name.startsWith("gatekeeper-"))
88:         .filter(name => {
89:       try {
90:         return statSync(join(parentDir, name, "wrangler.jsonc")).isFile();
91:       } catch {
92:         return false;
93:       }
94:     })
95:         .map(name => ({ name, dir: join(parentDir, name) }));
96:   } catch {
97:     return [];
98:   }
99: }
100: 
101: const gatekeepers = findGatekeepers(PACKAGES_DIR);
102: 
103: // The Context Library (packages/gatekeeper-context) is discovered by findGatekeepers and bound
104: // like any other gatekeeper (GATEKEEPER_CONTEXT -> GatekeeperVendor). Its describe() reports
105: // autoProvisionsAccount, so core auto-provisions one Context account per user. The only extra
106: // wiring it needs is a sharingDomain in its binding props (see below).
107: const CONTEXT_GATEKEEPER_NAME = "gatekeeper-context";

109: // What Wrangler picks for itself when no --port is derived, so also what we poll.
110: const DEFAULT_WRANGLER_PORT = 8787;
111: 
112: // Watchers rebuild each gatekeeper's generated UI (src/generated/*) on source change; wrangler dev's
113: // `watch_dir: src` then re-bundles the worker. Deferred ones start once Wrangler is listening.
114: const devWatchers: ChildProcess[] = [];
115: const deferredWatchers: (() => void)[] = [];
116: let stoppingDevWatchers = false;
117: let wranglerChild: ChildProcess | null = null;

119: // Resolve once something accepts a TCP connection on `port`, or once `timeoutMs` has elapsed.
120: function waitForPort(port: number, timeoutMs: number): Promise<void> {
121:   return new Promise<void>(resolve => {
122:     const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
123:     const attempt = () => {
124:       const socket = connect({ port, host: "127.0.0.1" });
125:       socket.once("connect", () => {
126:         socket.destroy();
127:         resolve();
128:       });
129:       socket.once("error", () => {
130:         socket.destroy();
131:         if (Date.now() >= deadline) resolve();
132:         else setTimeout(attempt, 100).unref();
133:       });
134:     };
135:     attempt();
136:   });
137: }

139: // Spawn a persistent watcher.
140: function spawnDevWatcher(label: string, command: string, args: string[]): void {
141:   const watcher = spawn(command, args, { stdio: "inherit", cwd: ROOT });
142:   watcher.on("exit", (code, signal) => {
143:     if (stoppingDevWatchers) return;
144:     console.error(`${label} exited unexpectedly (code=${code}, signal=${signal}).`);
145:   });
146:   devWatchers.push(watcher);
147: }
148: 
149: // No-op once shutdown has begun: reaching the port deadline just as the user hits Ctrl-C must not
150: // spawn a watcher that nothing is left to kill.
151: function startDeferredWatchers(): void {
152:   if (stoppingDevWatchers) return;
153:   for (const start of deferredWatchers.splice(0)) start();
154: }

156: function stopDevWatchers(): void {
157:   stoppingDevWatchers = true;

176: // Shutdown is driven by Wrangler's exit. Ctrl-C reaches the whole process group, so Wrangler is

179: // ineffective and leave this process waiting forever -- a second signal or the grace deadline
180: // escalates to SIGKILLing Wrangler's whole tree.
181: const FORCE_KILL_GRACE_MS = 10_000;
182: let receivedShutdownSignals = 0;
183: let forcingShutdown = false;
184: let shutdownExitCode: number | null = null;

186: async function forceKillWrangler(exitCode: number): Promise<void> {
187:   if (forcingShutdown) return;
188:   forcingShutdown = true;
189:   if (wranglerChild?.exitCode === null && wranglerChild.signalCode === null && wranglerChild.pid) {
190:     await killProcessTree(wranglerChild.pid, "SIGKILL").catch(() => {});

192:   process.exit(exitCode);

195: async function onShutdownSignal(signal: NodeJS.Signals, exitCode: number): Promise<void> {
196:   receivedShutdownSignals++;
197:   shutdownExitCode ??= exitCode;
198:   if (receivedShutdownSignals > 1) return forceKillWrangler(exitCode);
199:   // Awaited before Wrangler is signalled: this process stays alive waiting for Wrangler's exit, so
200:   // there is time for the process tree walks. Ctrl-C is group-delivered, but a targeted signal
201:   // (kill <pid>, IDE stop buttons) reaches only this process, so the pre-flight builds have to be
202:   // torn down here too and a live Wrangler has to be signalled explicitly -- on the Ctrl-C path
203:   // the forwarded signal lands during Wrangler's own teardown, which tolerates the repeat.
204:   await stopDevWatchersDeep();
205:   await stopPreflightBuilds();
206:   if (wranglerChild?.exitCode === null) {
207:     wranglerChild.kill(signal);
208:     setTimeout(() => forceKillWrangler(exitCode), FORCE_KILL_GRACE_MS).unref();
209:   } else {
210:     // Nothing left to wait for; without this exit the disabled default would keep us alive.
211:     process.exit(exitCode);
212:   }
213: }

236:   return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
237:     const child = spawn(command, args, { stdio: "inherit", cwd });
238:     preflightBuilds.add(child);
239:     child.on("error", error => {
240:       preflightBuilds.delete(child);

342: // Whether wrapping `path` in plain double quotes is safe in the shell that runs the rewritten

352: // through a shell, so a body chained with `&&` stays valid.
353: function withoutPnpmIndirection(pkgDir: string, command: string, depth = 0): string {
354:   const runScript = /^pnpm run ([\w:.@-]+)$/.exec(command.trim())?.[1];
355:   if (runScript && depth < 2) {

364:   return command.replaceAll(/\bpnpm exec ([\w@/.-]+)/g, (original, bin) => {
365:     const entry = resolveBinEntry(pkgDir, bin);

222: // task declares VITE_* as fingerprinted env — a release built at a different flag value is a cache

225:   const env = { ...process.env, VITE_CF_ACCESS_MODE: "true" };

233: // which is what makes these safe to overlap.
234: async function bundleWorker(pkg: DeployablePackage, bundleDir: string, signal: AbortSignal) {
235:   const outDir = join(bundleDir, pkg.name);
236:   await run(pkg.name, "pnpm", ["exec", "wrangler", "deploy", "--dry-run", "--outdir", outDir],

241: // Runs the frontend build and every worker bundle, and owns the scratch directory they bundle into
242: // for exactly as long as they need it: `collectModules` has read each bundle's bytes into memory by
243: // the time its task resolves, so nothing downstream reads the directory back.
244: //
245: // The frontend build and the worker bundles go all at once. Only a worker that serves static assets
246: // reads workshop-frontend/dist (the router points its `assets.directory` there), so it alone waits

248: // so a second asset-serving worker would be sequenced too.
249: //
250: // `frontend` is awaited by the allSettled as well as inside the task, so a frontend failure is
251: // observed even when no bundle got as far as awaiting it.
252: //
253: // Fail-fast: the first failure anywhere aborts the controller *with itself as the reason*, which
254: // stops mapConcurrent from claiming more bundles and kills the process trees of the commands
255: // already running (see `run`). Every task is still awaited -- allSettled, and mapConcurrent waits
256: // for its in-flight tasks -- so the run reports every real failure rather than whichever one lost
257: // the race, and it always reaches the cleanup below. What it does not claim is that every
258: // descendant is dead when a task settles; `run` says why that is tolerated. A cancelled command
259: // rejects with the abort reason, i.e. the root cause itself, which is what lets the failure summary
260: // below dedupe down to the real failures by identity.
261: async function buildAll(packages: DeployablePackage[], concurrency: number): Promise<{
262:   bundles: ReturnType<typeof collectModules>[];

265:   const controller = new AbortController();
266:   // One abort listener per running command (`run`), removed as each finishes. The default cap of 10

270:   const failFast = <T>(p: Promise<T>): Promise<T> =>

273:   // Termination from outside runs the same cancellation path a build failure does, which is the only
274:   // way the descendants get stopped and the scratch directory below gets removed. Installing these
275:   // also disables Node's default exit-on-signal, and that default is the whole problem: a *targeted*

279:   // anyway; nothing else is that kind.

283:   const onStopSignal = (signal: NodeJS.Signals) => {

286:     // signal started are what actually reach a descendant it has already reparented, so this cuts
287:     // their grace short and leaves with them rather than exiting out from under them -- bounded by

292:       forcing = true;
293:       forceKill.abort();

295:           child.pid === undefined ? null : killProcessTree(child.pid, "SIGKILL").catch(() => {}))])

300:             rmSync(bundleDir, { recursive: true, force: true });

314:     const frontend = failFast(buildFrontend(controller.signal));

320:       frontend,

324:           .filter((r) => r.status === "rejected")

342:     // and on POSIX its open files survive the unlink.

359:   const packages = readDeployablePackages(PACKAGES_DIR);
360: 
361:   // 1. Every bundle, overlapping.
362:   const { bundles, assets } = await buildAll(packages, args.concurrency);
363: 
364:   // 2. Everything below is ordered by package, so the release bytes do not depend on which build
365:   //    finished first.
366:   const assetVariants = { access: assets };
367:   for (const { blobs } of Object.values(assetVariants)) {
368:     for (const [hash, blob] of blobs) {
369:       writeFileSync(join(args.out, "assets", hash), blob.bytes);
370:     }
371:   }
372: 
373:   const workers: WorkerBuild[] = packages.map((pkg, i) => {
374:     const { mainModule, modules } = bundles[i];
375:     for (const mod of modules) {
376:       writeFileSync(join(args.out, "modules", mod.sha256), mod.bytes);
377:     }
378:     return {
379:       pkgName: pkg.name,
380:       config: pkg.config,
381:       mainModule,
382:       modules,
383:       deployInputs: readDeployInputs(pkg.dir),
384:     };
385:   });
386: 
387:   // 3. The manifest ties it together. Written last locally too, mirroring the R2 upload order
388:   //    (manifest presence == release complete).
389:   const manifest = generateManifest({
390:     releaseId,
391:     commit,
392:     createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
393:     wranglerVersion,
394:     workers,
395:     assetVariants,
396:   });
397:   writeFileSync(join(args.out, "manifest.json"), stableStringify(manifest) + "\n");
398: 
399:   const moduleCount = workers.reduce((n, w) => n + w.modules.length, 0);
400:   console.log(`\nrelease ${releaseId}: ${workers.length} workers, ${moduleCount} modules, ` +
401:       `${Object.keys(manifest.assets).length} unique asset blobs -> ${args.out}`);
402: }
403: 
404: try {
405:   await main();
406: } catch (error) {
407:   // A summary, not a stack: every failed command already printed its own diagnostics as a block,
408:   // and with the builds overlapping there can be more than one to name.
409:   const failures = error instanceof AggregateError ? error.errors : [error];
410:   // Cancelled from outside is not a broken build, and its exit code is the signal's. Checked over
411:   // the flattened list rather than `error` alone: the dedupe in buildAll collapses the reason every
412:   // cancelled command rejected with down to one, so the common case arrives bare -- but a real
413:   // failure racing the signal arrives as an AggregateError holding both.
414:   const cancelled = failures.find((f) => f instanceof CancelledBySignal);
415:   if (cancelled) {
416:     console.error(`\nrelease build ${cancelled.message}`);
417:     process.exitCode = cancelled.exitCode;
418:   } else {
419:     console.error("\nrelease build failed:");
420:     for (const failure of failures) {
421:       console.error(`  - ${failure instanceof Error ? failure.message : String(failure)}`);
422:     }
423:     process.exitCode = 1;
424:   }
425:   // Not process.exit(): every child has been awaited by now, so the event loop drains on its own
426:   // and piped stdio gets flushed rather than truncated mid-diagnostic.
427: }

6: // package's wrangler.jsonc and emits binding *templates* — every account-specific value replaced
7: // by a placeholder the deploy service resolves from instance state:
8: //
9: //   $ACCOUNT_ID              the user's account tag
10: //   $KV_<BINDING>_ID         a KV namespace provisioned at deploy time
11: //   $R2_<BINDING>_NAME       an R2 bucket provisioned at deploy time
12: //   $WORKER_NAME(<pkg>)      the instance's chosen name for another worker in this release
13: //   $SECRET(<name>)          a user-supplied secret, passed through as secret_text
14: //   $PUBLIC_BASE_URL         the instance's public origin (the router's URL)

16: // The placeholder list is closed: the deploy-side renderer fails on any `$` token it doesn't
17: // recognize, so this file and the renderer must evolve together (manifestVersion guards that).

24: /** Manifest version the deploy-side renderer must agree with (see header comment). */
25: export const MANIFEST_VERSION = 1;

27: /** A `{ binding: "NAME" }`-shaped wrangler binding declaration. */
28: export interface BindingDecl {
29:   binding: string;
30: }
31: 
32: /** A service binding declaration in a wrangler config. */
33: export interface ServiceBinding {
34:   /** Binding name the calling worker reads. */
35:   binding: string;
36:   /** Name of the worker being called. */
37:   service: string;
38:   /** RPC entrypoint on the target, when the caller uses one rather than plain HTTP. */
39:   entrypoint?: string;
40:   /** Props handed to the target worker on every call. */
41:   props?: Record<string, unknown>;

45:  * A worker's custom `build` stanza — the command wrangler runs before bundling. Shared with
46:  * `run-dev-server.ts`, which rewrites the command for dev.
47:  */
48: export interface WranglerBuild {
49:   /** Shell command wrangler runs. */
50:   command?: string;
51:   /** Directory the command runs in. Relative paths in it resolve against this. */
52:   cwd?: string;
53:   /** Paths whose changes re-run the command under `wrangler dev`. */
54:   watch_dir?: string | string[];
55: }

57: /**
58:  * Workers observability settings. Deliberately closed rather than carrying an index signature: a
59:  * new key in a deployable worker's wrangler.jsonc should surface here, the same way
60:  * `HANDLED_CONFIG_KEYS` makes an unrecognized top-level key fail the build.
61:  */
62: export interface ObservabilityConfig {
63:   /** Whether observability is on. */
64:   enabled: boolean;
65:   /** Fraction of requests sampled. */
66:   head_sampling_rate?: number;
67:   /** Nested log settings. */
68:   logs?: {
69:     enabled?: boolean;
70:     invocation_logs?: boolean;
71:     head_sampling_rate?: number;

73: }

76:  * One Durable Object migration step, verbatim from wrangler.jsonc. Only the operations the
77:  * deployable workers actually use are named; the index signature carries anything else through
78:  * untouched, since the manifest replays the history rather than interpreting it.
79:  */

81:   /** Migration tag. The final one is what re-PUTs of an existing worker must present. */
82:   tag: string;
83:   /** Classes introduced with SQLite-backed storage. */
84:   new_sqlite_classes?: string[];
85:   [key: string]: unknown;
86: }

89:  * The subset of a deployable worker's `wrangler.jsonc` this pipeline reads. Shared by the manifest
90:  * generator, `build-release.ts` and the preview-config generator, so all three agree on the shape.
91:  * Deliberately partial and loose: `buildWorkerEntry` fails closed on any key not in
92:  * `HANDLED_CONFIG_KEYS`, which is the real guard against a config shape nobody has decided about.
93:  */
94: export interface WranglerConfig {
95:   /** Worker name as deployed by `wrangler deploy` from this package. */
96:   name?: string;
97:   /** Entry module path, relative to the package directory. */
98:   main?: string;
99:   /** Workers runtime compatibility date. */
100:   compatibility_date?: string;
101:   /** Workers runtime compatibility flags. */
102:   compatibility_flags?: string[];
103:   /** Durable Object migration history, ordered. Replayed verbatim by fresh installs. */
104:   migrations?: DurableObjectMigration[];
105:   /** Workers observability settings. */
106:   observability?: ObservabilityConfig;
107:   /** KV namespace bindings; ids become `$KV_<BINDING>_ID` placeholders. */
108:   kv_namespaces?: BindingDecl[];
109:   /** R2 bucket bindings; names become `$R2_<BINDING>_NAME` placeholders. */
110:   r2_buckets?: BindingDecl[];
111:   /** Worker Loader bindings (the Gadget sandbox). */
112:   worker_loaders?: BindingDecl[];
113:   /** Service bindings; targets become `$WORKER_NAME(<pkg>)` placeholders. */
114:   services?: ServiceBinding[];
115:   /** Browser Rendering binding (Gadget PDF exports). */
116:   browser?: BindingDecl;
117:   /** Artifacts binding — closed beta, cut from customer manifests. */
118:   artifacts?: BindingDecl;
119:   /** Static-asset serving config (the router). */
120:   assets?: {
121:     binding?: string;
122:     directory?: string;
123:     not_found_handling?: string;
124:     run_worker_first?: string[];

126:   /** Plain-text vars, passed through and extended with per-kind template vars. */
127:   vars?: Record<string, unknown>;
128:   /** Custom build command wrangler runs before bundling. */
129:   build?: WranglerBuild;
130:   /** Module resolution rules for non-JS imports. */
131:   rules?: unknown[];
132:   /** Present in the files but ignored. */
133:   $schema?: string;
134: }
135: 
136: /** A deployable workspace package and its parsed Wrangler configuration. */
137: export interface DeployablePackage {
138:   /** Package directory name, which is also the worker name. */
139:   name: string;
140:   /** Absolute path to the package directory. */
141:   dir: string;
142:   /** The package's parsed wrangler.jsonc. */
143:   config: WranglerConfig;
144: }
145: 
146: /** One user-supplied value the deploy wizard collects before installing a gatekeeper. */
147: export interface DeployInput {
148:   /** Env var / secret name the worker reads. Screaming snake case. */
149:   name: string;
150:   /** How the deploy service supplies it. Secrets become `secret_text` bindings. */
151:   kind: "secret" | "var" | "workerName";
152:   /** Wizard field label. */
153:   label: string;
154:   /** Optional longer help text shown under the field. */
155:   help?: string;
156:   /** Link to the third-party console page where the value is found. */
157:   consoleUrl?: string;
158:   /** Ordered setup steps shown alongside the field. */
159:   setupSteps?: string[];
160:   /** Redirect URI to show the user, with `$PUBLIC_BASE_URL` still unresolved. */
161:   redirectUriTemplate?: string;
162: }
163: 
164: /** A rendered binding in a worker's manifest entry; account-specific values are placeholders. */
165: export type ManifestBinding = { type: string; name: string } & Record<string, unknown>;
166: 
167: /** Everything the manifest says about one worker in the release. */
168: export interface WorkerEntry {
169:   /** Which role this worker plays in a deployment. */
170:   kind: "backend" | "router" | "gatekeeper";
171:   /** Gatekeepers only: the path segment the router routes `/gatekeeper/<shortName>/*` on. */
172:   shortName?: string;
173:   /** Whether the deploy wizard offers this worker for installation. */
174:   installable: boolean;
175:   /** Installed server-side on every fresh core deploy, with no user interaction. */
176:   preinstall?: true;
177:   /** Installable at most once per instance. */
178:   singleton?: true;
179:   /** Name of the ESM entry module within `modules`. */
180:   mainModule: string;
181:   /** Every uploadable module, content-addressed. */
182:   modules: { name: string; type: string; sha256: string; size: number; r2Key: string }[];
183:   /** Workers runtime compatibility date. */
184:   compatibilityDate: string | undefined;
185:   /** Workers runtime compatibility flags. */
186:   compatibilityFlags: string[];
187:   /** Full ordered migration history, verbatim from wrangler.jsonc. */
188:   migrations: DurableObjectMigration[];
189:   /** Binding templates for the deploy-side renderer. */
190:   bindings: ManifestBinding[];
191:   /** Plain-text vars, including the per-kind templated ones. */
192:   vars: Record<string, unknown>;
193:   /** Workers observability settings. */
194:   observability: ObservabilityConfig;
195:   /** How the deploy service expands installed gatekeepers into `GATEKEEPER_*` bindings. */
196:   gatekeeperBindingExpansion?: {
197:     entrypoint?: string;
198:     propsByPackage: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>;
199:   };
200:   /** Static-asset serving config, with one manifest per asset variant. */
201:   assetsConfig?: {
202:     not_found_handling: string | undefined;
203:     run_worker_first: string[] | undefined;
204:     variants: Record<string, { manifest: Record<string, AssetManifestEntry> }>;
205:   };
206:   /** Values the deploy wizard collects before installing. Absent for core workers. */
207:   inputs?: DeployInput[];
208: }
209: 
210: /** The release manifest: the contract between this repo's CI and the deploy service. */
211: export interface ReleaseManifest {
212:   /** Guards the closed placeholder list against renderer drift. */
213:   manifestVersion: number;
214:   /** Immutable release id; the R2 prefix everything lands under. */
215:   releaseId: string;
216:   /** Full commit SHA the release was built from. */
217:   commit: string;
218:   /** ISO-8601 build time. */
219:   createdAt: string;
220:   /** Version of the pinned wrangler that produced every bundle. */
221:   wranglerVersion: string;
222:   /** Per-package worker entries. */
223:   workers: Record<string, WorkerEntry>;
224:   /** Every unique asset blob in the release, keyed by content hash. */
225:   assets: Record<string, { size: number; r2Key: string }>;
226: }
227: 
228: /** One worker's build products, as handed to {@link generateManifest}. */
229: export interface WorkerBuild {
230:   /** Workspace package directory name, e.g. `gatekeeper-google`. */
231:   pkgName: string;
232:   /** The package's parsed wrangler.jsonc. */
233:   config: WranglerConfig;
234:   /** Name of the ESM entry module within `modules`. */
235:   mainModule: string;
236:   /** Every uploadable module from the dry-run bundle. */
237:   modules: CollectedModule[];
238:   /** Contents of the package's `deploy-inputs.json`, if it has one. */
239:   deployInputs?: DeployInput[];
240: }
241: 
242: // wrangler.jsonc keys this generator understands. Anything else fails closed — a new config key
243: // on a deployable worker needs an explicit decision about how customer instances get it.
244: const HANDLED_CONFIG_KEYS = new Set([
245:   "$schema", "name", "main", "build", "compatibility_date", "compatibility_flags", "rules",
246:   "migrations", "observability", "kv_namespaces", "r2_buckets", "worker_loaders", "services",
247:   "assets", "vars",
248:   // Browser Rendering (Gadget PDF exports). Unlike artifacts it is generally available, so it
249:   // passes through to customer instances as a placeholder-free binding, like the AI binding.
250:   "browser",
251:   // gatekeeper-context's Artifacts binding is closed-beta and cannot be provisioned in arbitrary
252:   // user accounts; it is dropped from customer manifests (the gatekeeper degrades gracefully).
253:   "artifacts",
254: ]);
255: 
256: const ARTIFACTS_CUT_ALLOWED = new Set(["gatekeeper-context"]);
257: 
258: // Installable gatekeepers that do NOT take third-party OAuth app credentials; everyone else
259: // defaults to CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET secret inputs (overridable via deploy-inputs.json).
260: const NO_DEFAULT_CRED_INPUTS = new Set([
261:   "gatekeeper-context",       // no third-party service; uses its own storage
262:   "gatekeeper-homeassistant", // users connect their own Home Assistant URL + token in-app
263:   "gatekeeper-scheduler",     // auto-provisioned; no third-party OAuth app
264:   "gatekeeper-mcp",           // MCP OAuth uses dynamic client registration, not a static app
265:   "gatekeeper-mcp-portal",    // same MCP OAuth chain as gatekeeper-mcp
266: ]);
267: 
268: // Not installable on customer instances: Email Routing needs a zone, which workers.dev-hosted
269: // instances don't have. The bundle still ships in the release so the entry stays auditable.
270: const NOT_INSTALLABLE = new Set(["gatekeeper-email"]);
271: 
272: // Ambient gatekeepers the deploy service installs on every fresh core deploy, server-side with
273: // no user interaction. Members must take no inputs of any kind (enforced below): a preinstall
274: // has nobody to ask.
275: const PREINSTALL = new Set(["gatekeeper-context", "gatekeeper-scheduler"]);
276: 
277: // Gatekeepers that may be installed at most once per instance; the deploy service enforces this
278: // at install time. The giveaway is the account declaring an agent singleton
279: // (`AccountDescription.singleton` — context's `ContextLibrary`, scheduler's `ScheduleSession`):
280: // the Workshop auto-provisions those accounts and folds the singleton into every workspace as an
281: // ambient gatekeeper, so a second install would hand every user a duplicate ambient capsule.
282: // Independent of PREINSTALL in principle; the two sets coincide today only because every ambient
283: // gatekeeper we ship is also preinstalled.
284: const SINGLETON = new Set(["gatekeeper-context", "gatekeeper-scheduler"]);
285: 
286: /** Default wizard inputs for an installable gatekeeper that fronts a third-party OAuth app. */
287: export const DEFAULT_CRED_INPUTS: DeployInput[] = [
288:   {
289:     name: "CLIENT_ID",
290:     kind: "secret",
291:     label: "OAuth client ID",
292:   },
293:   {
294:     name: "CLIENT_SECRET",
295:     kind: "secret",
296:     label: "OAuth client secret",
297:   },
298: ];
299: 
300: const GATEKEEPER_PREFIX = "gatekeeper-";
301: 
302: /** Read every deployable package and its Wrangler configuration, sorted by package name. */
303: export function readDeployablePackages(packagesDir: string): DeployablePackage[] {
304:   return readdirSync(packagesDir)
305:       .filter((name) => {
306:     try {
307:       return statSync(join(packagesDir, name, "wrangler.jsonc")).isFile();
308:     } catch {
309:       return false;
310:     }
311:   })
312:       .toSorted()
313:       .map((name) => {
314:     const dir = join(packagesDir, name);
315:     const config = parse(readFileSync(join(dir, "wrangler.jsonc"), "utf8")) as WranglerConfig;
316:     return { name, dir, config };
317:   });
318: }
319: 
320: /** True when a deployable package is a gatekeeper worker. */
321: export function isGatekeeperPackage(pkgName: string): boolean {
322:   return pkgName.startsWith(GATEKEEPER_PREFIX);
323: }
324: 
325: /** Return a gatekeeper package's vendor id used in its routed URL. */
326: export function gatekeeperShortName(pkgName: string): string {
327:   return pkgName.slice(GATEKEEPER_PREFIX.length);
328: }
329: 
330: /** Read a package's `deploy-inputs.json`, or undefined if it declares none. */
331: export function readDeployInputs(pkgDir: string): DeployInput[] | undefined {
332:   const path = join(pkgDir, "deploy-inputs.json");
333:   if (!existsSync(path)) return undefined;
334:   return JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8")) as DeployInput[];
335: }
336: 
337: function workerKind(pkgName: string): WorkerEntry["kind"] {
338:   if (pkgName === "workshop-backend") return "backend";
339:   if (pkgName === "router") return "router";
340:   if (isGatekeeperPackage(pkgName)) return "gatekeeper";
341:   throw new Error(`cannot classify deployable package: ${pkgName}`);
342: }
343: 
344: /**
345:  * Builds one worker's manifest entry from its parsed wrangler.jsonc and collected modules.
346:  * `modules` entries are { name, type, sha256, size } (bytes stripped by the caller).
347:  */
348: export function buildWorkerEntry(
349:   { pkgName, config, mainModule, modules, deployInputs }: WorkerBuild,
350: ): WorkerEntry {
351:   const kind = workerKind(pkgName);
352:   const unknownKeys = Object.keys(config).filter((k) => !HANDLED_CONFIG_KEYS.has(k));
353:   if (unknownKeys.length > 0) {
354:     throw new Error(`${pkgName}/wrangler.jsonc has key(s) this generator doesn't handle: ` +
355:         unknownKeys.join(", "));
356:   }
357:   if (config.artifacts && !ARTIFACTS_CUT_ALLOWED.has(pkgName)) {
358:     throw new Error(`${pkgName} declares an artifacts binding; only gatekeeper-context's is ` +
359:         `known (and cut). Decide how customer instances should handle this one.`);
360:   }
361: 
362:   const bindings: ManifestBinding[] = [];
363:   const vars: Record<string, unknown> = {};
364: 
365:   for (const kv of config.kv_namespaces ?? []) {
366:     bindings.push({
367:       type: "kv_namespace",
368:       name: kv.binding,
369:       namespace_id: `$KV_${kv.binding}_ID`,
370:     });
371:   }
372:   for (const r2 of config.r2_buckets ?? []) {
373:     bindings.push({
374:       type: "r2_bucket",
375:       name: r2.binding,
376:       bucket_name: `$R2_${r2.binding}_NAME`,
377:     });
378:   }
379:   if (config.browser) {
380:     // `remote` is dev-only wrangler behavior; the deployed binding is just { type, name }.
381:     bindings.push({ type: "browser", name: config.browser.binding });
382:   }
383:   for (const loader of config.worker_loaders ?? []) {
384:     bindings.push({ type: "worker_loader", name: loader.binding });
385:   }
386:   for (const svc of config.services ?? []) {
387:     bindings.push({
388:       type: "service",
389:       name: svc.binding,
390:       service: `$WORKER_NAME(${svc.service})`,
391:       ...(svc.entrypoint ? { entrypoint: svc.entrypoint } : {}),
392:     });
393:   }
394: 
395:   let assetsConfig: WorkerEntry["assetsConfig"];
396:   if (config.assets) {
397:     bindings.push({ type: "assets", name: config.assets.binding ?? "ASSETS" });
398:     assetsConfig = {
399:       not_found_handling: config.assets.not_found_handling,
400:       run_worker_first: config.assets.run_worker_first,
401:       // Filled by the caller (build-release) with
402:       // { access: { manifest: { "/path": { hash, size } } } }.
403:       variants: {},
404:     };
405:   }
406: 
407:   Object.assign(vars, config.vars ?? {});
408: 
409:   // Per-kind template vars, mirroring what generate-wrangler-prod.js hand-codes internally
410:   // (PUBLIC_BASE_URL on the backend; per-gatekeeper BASE_URL under the shared origin).
411:   let inputs: DeployInput[] | undefined;
412:   let installable = true;
413:   let gatekeeperBindingExpansion: WorkerEntry["gatekeeperBindingExpansion"];
414:   if (kind === "backend") {
415:     // Deliberate contract: the manifest carries only $PUBLIC_BASE_URL. The backend's other
416:     // instance-state vars (ADMINS, DEPLOY_URL, CF_ACCESS_*, CF_AI_GATEWAY*) are injected by
417:     // the deploy service's backendExtraVars at PUT time, never manifest-templated.
418:     vars.PUBLIC_BASE_URL = "$PUBLIC_BASE_URL";
419:     // Every deployed backend gets the Workers AI binding (hardcoded like PUBLIC_BASE_URL, not
420:     // read from wrangler.jsonc): webFetch's toMarkdown conversion depends on it, and it is also
421:     // the backend's default AI Gateway transport (the deploy service creates the gateway in the
422:     // user's own account, so the in-account requirement holds; CF_AI_GATEWAY_USE_BINDING=false
423:     // is the cross-account opt-out) — binding requests are pre-authenticated, so inference and
424:     // cost-log reads need no CF_AI_GATEWAY_API_TOKEN (google provider excepted).
425:     // No placeholders — the deploy renderer passes it through.
426:     bindings.push({ type: "ai", name: "WORKERS_AI" });
427:     // Installed gatekeepers are called through GATEKEEPER_* service bindings with the
428:     // GatekeeperVendor entrypoint (same shape run-dev-server.ts generates for dev).
429:     gatekeeperBindingExpansion = {
430:       entrypoint: "GatekeeperVendor",
431:       // gatekeeper-context namespaces each workshop's shared data by a sharingDomain carried in
432:       // binding props; the instance's public origin is the natural stable value.
433:       propsByPackage: {
434:         "gatekeeper-context": { sharingDomain: "$PUBLIC_BASE_URL" },
435:       },
436:     };
437:   } else if (kind === "router") {
438:     // The router routes /gatekeeper/<short>/* by scanning its own GATEKEEPER_* bindings
439:     // (default entrypoint — it forwards whole HTTP requests, not vendor RPC).
440:     gatekeeperBindingExpansion = { propsByPackage: {} };
441:   } else {
442:     vars.BASE_URL = `$PUBLIC_BASE_URL/gatekeeper/${gatekeeperShortName(pkgName)}`;
443:     installable = !NOT_INSTALLABLE.has(pkgName);
444:     if (installable) {
445:       inputs = deployInputs ??
446:           (NO_DEFAULT_CRED_INPUTS.has(pkgName) ? [] : DEFAULT_CRED_INPUTS);
447:     } else {
448:       inputs = [];
449:     }
450:     // Every declared secret input becomes a pass-through secret_text binding.
451:     for (const input of inputs) {
452:       if (input.kind === "secret") {
453:         bindings.push({ type: "secret_text", name: input.name, text: `$SECRET(${input.name})` });
454:       }
455:     }
456:     if (PREINSTALL.has(pkgName) && inputs.length > 0) {
457:       throw new Error(`${pkgName} is preinstalled but declares input(s); preinstalls run ` +
458:           `with no user interaction, so this release would be broken`);
459:     }
460:   }
461: 
462:   return {
463:     kind,

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: 
3: // Mirrors a built release directory (see build-release.ts) to R2 via the S3 API.
4: //
5: // Blobs are content-addressed, so unchanged files dedupe across releases: each key is HEAD'd
6: // first and skipped if present. The manifest is uploaded LAST — its presence under
7: // releases/<id>/manifest.json is what marks a release complete, so a crashed upload never
8: // leaves a manifest pointing at missing blobs.
9: //
10: // With --candidate the manifest lands under candidates/<id>/manifest.json instead — invisible
11: // to the deploy service (which scans only releases/) until promote-release.ts copies it over
12: // after the e2e gate passes. Blob handling is identical either way.
13: //
14: // Env: R2_ENDPOINT (https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com), R2_BUCKET,
15: //      R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
16: // Usage: node scripts/release/upload-release.ts --release <dir> [--candidate]
17: 
18: import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";
19: import { join, resolve } from "node:path";
20: import { AwsClient } from "aws4fetch";
21: import { assetR2Key, moduleR2Key, type ReleaseManifest } from "./manifest-lib.ts";
22: 
23: const UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY = 8;
24: 
25: function requireEnv(name: string): string {
26:   const value = process.env[name];
27:   if (!value) throw new Error(`missing required environment variable: ${name}`);
28:   return value;
29: }
30: 
31: function parseArgs(argv: string[]): { release: string; candidate: boolean } {
32:   let release: string | undefined;
33:   let candidate = false;
34:   for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
35:     if (argv[i] === "--release") release = resolve(argv[++i]);
36:     else if (argv[i] === "--candidate") candidate = true;
37:     else throw new Error(`unknown argument: ${argv[i]}`);
38:   }
39:   if (!release) throw new Error("--release <dir> is required");
40:   return { release, candidate };
41: }
42: 
43: async function main() {
44:   const args = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
45:   const endpoint = requireEnv("R2_ENDPOINT").replace(/\/$/, "");
46:   const bucket = requireEnv("R2_BUCKET");
47:   const client = new AwsClient({
48:     accessKeyId: requireEnv("R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID"),
49:     secretAccessKey: requireEnv("R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"),
50:     service: "s3",
51:     region: "auto",
52:   });
53:   const keyUrl = (key: string) => `${endpoint}/${bucket}/${key}`;
54: 
55:   const manifest = JSON.parse(
56:       readFileSync(join(args.release, "manifest.json"), "utf8")) as ReleaseManifest;
57: 
58:   const blobs = [
59:     ...readdirSync(join(args.release, "modules")).map((sha256) => ({
60:       key: moduleR2Key(sha256),
61:       path: join(args.release, "modules", sha256),
62:     })),
63:     ...readdirSync(join(args.release, "assets")).map((hash) => ({
64:       key: assetR2Key(hash),
65:       path: join(args.release, "assets", hash),
66:     })),
67:   ];
68: 
69:   let uploaded = 0;
70:   let skipped = 0;
71:   const queue = [...blobs];
72:   async function worker() {
73:     for (;;) {
74:       const blob = queue.shift();
75:       if (!blob) return;
76:       const head = await client.fetch(keyUrl(blob.key), { method: "HEAD" });
77:       if (head.status === 200) {
78:         skipped++;
79:         continue;
80:       }
81:       if (head.status !== 404) {
82:         throw new Error(`HEAD ${blob.key}: unexpected status ${head.status}`);
83:       }
84:       const put = await client.fetch(keyUrl(blob.key), {
85:         method: "PUT",
86:         body: readFileSync(blob.path),
87:       });
88:       if (!put.ok) {
89:         throw new Error(`PUT ${blob.key}: ${put.status} ${await put.text()}`);
90:       }
91:       uploaded++;
92:     }
93:   }
94:   await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY }, worker));
95:   console.log(`blobs: ${uploaded} uploaded, ${skipped} already present`);
96: 
97:   const manifestKey =
98:     `${args.candidate ? "candidates" : "releases"}/${manifest.releaseId}/manifest.json`;
99:   const put = await client.fetch(keyUrl(manifestKey), {
100:     method: "PUT",
101:     body: readFileSync(join(args.release, "manifest.json")),
102:     headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
103:   });
104:   if (!put.ok) {
105:     throw new Error(`PUT ${manifestKey}: ${put.status} ${await put.text()}`);
106:   }
107:   console.log(args.candidate
108:     ? `candidate uploaded (not yet visible to the deploy service): ${manifestKey}`
109:     : `release complete: ${manifestKey}`);
110: }

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: 
3: // Promotes an e2e-verified candidate release: copies candidates/<id>/manifest.json to
4: // releases/<id>/manifest.json. The blobs are already in place — content-addressed and uploaded
5: // by upload-release.ts before its manifest PUT — so publishing is this single manifest copy.
6: // The copy is all-or-nothing (manifest-last protocol: the deploy service scans only releases/),
7: // but NOT isolated: the newer-release guard below is check-then-act, so concurrent promotions
8: // could still interleave between its LIST and the copy. The caller must serialize runs of this
9: // script — gadgets-internal's CI runs it in a resource group — and the guard then catches the
10: // remaining hazard, a promote that starts after a newer release has already published.
11: //
12: // Exit-0 guards (benign races must not fail the pipeline):
13: //   - already promoted: releases/<id>/manifest.json exists (idempotent re-runs)
14: //   - superseded: a CI-format id (r<run#>-<sha>) with a HIGHER run number already exists under
15: //     releases/. "Latest" is decided by manifest upload time (deploy's release.ts), so promoting
16: //     an older candidate after a newer one shipped would ROLL PRODUCTION BACK — the stale PUT
17: //     would carry the newest timestamp.
18: //
19: // A missing candidate manifest is a hard error: the caller asked to promote something that was
20: // never uploaded (or was cleaned up), and silently succeeding would report a phantom publish.
21: //
22: // Env: R2_ENDPOINT (https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com), R2_BUCKET,
23: //      R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
24: // Usage: node scripts/release/promote-release.ts --release-id <id>
25: 
26: import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
27: import { AwsClient } from "aws4fetch";
28: 
29: /** The CI run number of an `r<run#>-<sha>` release id, or null for any other id shape
30:  *  (dev-<ts> releases carry no ordering claim). */
31: export function ciRunNumber(releaseId: string): number | null {
32:   const match = /^r(\d+)-/.exec(releaseId);
33:   return match ? Number(match[1]) : null;
34: }
35: 
36: /** The already-published CI release id that supersedes this candidate, or null. Non-CI ids
37:  *  (either side) never participate: only run numbers are comparable. */
38: export function supersededBy(candidateId: string, publishedIds: Iterable<string>): string | null {
39:   const candidateRun = ciRunNumber(candidateId);
40:   if (candidateRun === null) return null;
41:   for (const id of publishedIds) {
42:     const run = ciRunNumber(id);
43:     if (run !== null && run > candidateRun) return id;
44:   }
45:   return null;
46: }
47: 
48: function requireEnv(name: string): string {
49:   const value = process.env[name];
50:   if (!value) throw new Error(`missing required environment variable: ${name}`);
51:   return value;
52: }
53: 
54: function parseArgs(argv: string[]): { releaseId: string } {
55:   let releaseId: string | undefined;
56:   for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
57:     if (argv[i] === "--release-id") releaseId = argv[++i];
58:     else throw new Error(`unknown argument: ${argv[i]}`);
59:   }
60:   if (!releaseId) throw new Error("--release-id <id> is required");
61:   return { releaseId };
62: }

65: // never fetched.

67:   client: AwsClient,

69: ): Promise<string[]> {

76:     if (!response.ok) {

78:     }
79:     const xml = await response.text();
80:     for (const match of xml.matchAll(/<Key>releases\/([^<]+)\/manifest\.json<\/Key>/g)) {
81:       ids.push(match[1]);
82:     }
83:     token = /<NextContinuationToken>([^<]+)<\/NextContinuationToken>/.exec(xml)?.[1];
84:   } while (token);
85:   return ids;
86: }
87:

89:   const args = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
90:   const endpoint = requireEnv("R2_ENDPOINT").replace(/\/$/, "");
91:   const bucket = requireEnv("R2_BUCKET");
92:   const client = new AwsClient({
93:     accessKeyId: requireEnv("R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID"),
94:     secretAccessKey: requireEnv("R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"),
95:     service: "s3",
96:     region: "auto",
97:   });
98:   const keyUrl = (key: string) => `${endpoint}/${bucket}/${key}`;
99: 
100:   const publishedKey = `releases/${args.releaseId}/manifest.json`;
101:   const candidateKey = `candidates/${args.releaseId}/manifest.json`;
102: 
103:   const publishedHead = await client.fetch(keyUrl(publishedKey), { method: "HEAD" });
104:   if (publishedHead.status === 200) {
105:     console.log(`already promoted: ${publishedKey}`);
106:     return;
107:   }
108:   if (publishedHead.status !== 404) {
109:     throw new Error(`HEAD ${publishedKey}: unexpected status ${publishedHead.status}`);
110:   }
111: 
112:   const candidate = await client.fetch(keyUrl(candidateKey), { method: "GET" });
113:   if (candidate.status === 404) {
114:     throw new Error(`candidate not found: ${candidateKey} — was the release uploaded ` +
115:       "with --candidate?");
116:   }
117:   if (!candidate.ok) {
118:     throw new Error(`GET ${candidateKey}: ${candidate.status} ${await candidate.text()}`);
119:   }
120:   const manifestBody = new Uint8Array(await candidate.arrayBuffer());
121: 
122:   const superseder = supersededBy(args.releaseId, await listPublishedReleaseIds(client, keyUrl));

1: // Hashing and bundle-collection helpers for release publishing.
2: //
3: // Two distinct hash schemes coexist on purpose:
4: //  - Worker modules are content-addressed by full SHA-256 (hex) — our own scheme, used for R2
5: //    dedupe and for auditing that a deployed bundle matches what CI built.
6: //  - Static assets use the Workers assets-upload API's content key: SHA-256 of
7: //    (base64(contents) + extension), hex, truncated to 32 chars. The dash computes exactly this
8: //    (stratus workers-and-pages/utils/assets.ts); the API treats it as an opaque per-file key, so
9: //    CI and the deploy service must agree on it byte for byte.
10: 
11: import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
12: import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
13: import { join, relative, extname, sep } from "node:path";
14: 
15: /** A worker module as collected from a dry-run bundle, before the manifest strips `bytes`. */
16: export interface CollectedModule {
17:   /** Module path relative to the bundle directory, POSIX-separated. */
18:   name: string;
19:   /** Module type the script-upload API understands (`esm`, `text`, `wasm`, `data`). */
20:   type: ModuleType;
21:   /** Full SHA-256 of the contents, hex — the module's content address. */
22:   sha256: string;
23:   /** Byte length. */
24:   size: number;
25:   /** The contents. Stripped before the module reaches the manifest. */
26:   bytes: Buffer;
27: }
28: 
29: /** One static asset's entry in the assets-upload-session manifest. */
30: export interface AssetManifestEntry {
31:   /** The Workers static-asset content key (see {@link cfAssetHash}). */
32:   hash: string;
33:   /** Byte length. */
34:   size: number;
35: }
36: 
37: /** A built static-asset directory: the upload-session manifest plus deduped blobs. */
38: export interface CollectedAssets {
39:   /** `{ "/path": { hash, size } }`, in the exact shape the assets-upload-session API takes. */
40:   manifest: Record<string, AssetManifestEntry>;
41:   /** Deduped contents, keyed by content hash, for content-addressed storage. */
42:   blobs: Map<string, { bytes: Buffer; size: number }>;
43: }
44: 
45: export function sha256Hex(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
46:   return createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
47: }
48: 
49: /** The Workers static-asset content key (see header comment). */
50: export function cfAssetHash(bytes: Uint8Array, filePath: string): string {
51:   const base64 = Buffer.from(bytes).toString("base64");
52:   const extension = extname(filePath).slice(1);
53:   return createHash("sha256").update(base64 + extension, "utf8").digest("hex").slice(0, 32);
54: }
55: 
56: // Module types understood by the script-upload API, keyed by file extension. The manifest
57: // records the type; the deploy service maps it to the multipart part's MIME type.
58: const MODULE_TYPE_BY_EXTENSION = {
59:   ".js": "esm",
60:   ".mjs": "esm",
61:   ".txt": "text",
62:   ".svg": "text",
63:   ".wasm": "wasm",
64:   ".bin": "data",
65: } as const satisfies Record<string, string>;
66: 
67: /** Module type recorded in the manifest, as understood by the script-upload API. */
68: export type ModuleType = (typeof MODULE_TYPE_BY_EXTENSION)[keyof typeof MODULE_TYPE_BY_EXTENSION];
69: 
70: // Files `wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir` writes that are not uploadable modules.
71: function isNonModuleFile(name: string): boolean {
72:   return name.endsWith(".map") || name === "README.md";
73: }
74: 
75: /**
76:  * Reads a `wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir` output directory and returns
77:  * `{ mainModule, modules }` where modules is sorted by name and each entry is
78:  * `{ name, type, sha256, size, bytes }`. Fails closed: an extension we don't recognize means a
79:  * bundle shape this pipeline has never seen, and needs an explicit decision rather than a guess.
80:  */
81: export function collectModules(outDir: string): {
82:   mainModule: string;
83:   modules: CollectedModule[];
84: } {
85:   const unsorted: CollectedModule[] = [];
86:   for (const file of walkFiles(outDir)) {
87:     const name = relative(outDir, file).split(sep).join("/");
88:     if (isNonModuleFile(name)) continue;
89:     const type: ModuleType | undefined =
90:         MODULE_TYPE_BY_EXTENSION[extname(name) as keyof typeof MODULE_TYPE_BY_EXTENSION];
91:     if (!type) {
92:       throw new Error(`unrecognized module file in dry-run output: ${name} (${outDir})`);
93:     }
94:     const bytes = readFileSync(file);
95:     unsorted.push({ name, type, sha256: sha256Hex(bytes), size: bytes.length, bytes });
96:   }
97:   const modules = unsorted.toSorted((a, b) => (a.name < b.name ? -1 : 1));
98: 
99:   const esmModules = modules.filter((m) => m.type === "esm");
100:   if (esmModules.length !== 1) {
101:     throw new Error(
102:         `expected exactly one ESM module in ${outDir}, found: ` +
103:         `${esmModules.map((m) => m.name).join(", ") || "(none)"}`);
104:   }
105:   return { mainModule: esmModules[0].name, modules };
106: }
107: 
108: /**
109:  * Reads a built static-asset directory and returns `{ manifest, blobs }`:
110:  *  - manifest: { "/path": { hash, size } } in the exact shape the assets-upload-session API takes
111:  *  - blobs: Map<hash, { bytes, size }> for content-addressed storage
112:  */
113: export function collectAssets(distDir: string): CollectedAssets {
114:   const manifest: Record<string, AssetManifestEntry> = {};
115:   const blobs = new Map<string, { bytes: Buffer; size: number }>();
116:   for (const file of walkFiles(distDir)) {
117:     const path = "/" + relative(distDir, file).split(sep).join("/");
118:     const bytes = readFileSync(file);
119:     const hash = cfAssetHash(bytes, file);
120:     manifest[path] = { hash, size: bytes.length };
121:     if (!blobs.has(hash)) blobs.set(hash, { bytes, size: bytes.length });
122:   }
123:   return { manifest, blobs };
124: }
125: 
126: function walkFiles(dir: string): string[] {
127:   const out: string[] = [];
128:   for (const name of readdirSync(dir).toSorted()) {
129:     const path = join(dir, name);
130:     if (statSync(path).isDirectory()) {
131:       out.push(...walkFiles(path));
132:     } else {
133:       out.push(path);
134:     }
135:   }
136:   return out;
137: }
138: 
139: /**
140:  * JSON.stringify with all object keys sorted, so manifests diff cleanly and the golden-manifest
141:  * test is byte-stable. Arrays keep their order (migration history is ordered!).
142:  */
143: export function stableStringify(value: unknown, indent = 2): string {
144:   return JSON.stringify(sortKeysDeep(value), null, indent);
145: }
146: 
147: function sortKeysDeep(value: unknown): unknown {
148:   if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(sortKeysDeep);
149:   if (value && typeof value === "object") {
150:     const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
151:     for (const key of Object.keys(value).toSorted()) {
152:       out[key] = sortKeysDeep((value as Record<string, unknown>)[key]);
153:     }
154:     return out;
155:   }
156:   return value;
157: }

12: // Deployment runs in three tiers, because each tier's service bindings must name the previews the
13: // tier before it produced:
14: //
15: //   1. the 16 gatekeepers  (concurrently; nothing binds to anything)
16: //   2. workshop-backend    (binds every gatekeeper preview via GatekeeperVendor)
17: //   3. router              (binds the backend preview and every gatekeeper preview, and owns the
18: //                           public origin: it serves the frontend and proxies /api and
19: //                           /gatekeeper/<short>)
20: //
21: // Between tiers the next tier's `previews.services[].preview_id` is patched with the ids the
22: // previous tier returned. Everything else — every URL in the config — is derived up front from
23: // the router's preview name, which is deterministic, so the tiers only have to exchange ids.
24: //
25: // The router is the only one of the eighteen with a hostname. Preview URLs are public, so the
26: // other seventeen set `preview_urls: false` and are reached over service bindings alone; the
27: // deploy asserts that, since a URL appearing on one of them is a way around the router.
28: //
29: // The backend's secrets — its admins and the Cloudflare Access application that authenticates the
30: // instance — are uploaded to the worker's Previews settings between tiers 1 and 2 and are never
31: // written into a config, because Wrangler prints config values and this workflow's logs are public.
32: // See uploadSecrets, and backendSecrets in staging-config.ts.

123: const USAGE = "Usage: preview.ts <config|deploy|delete|sweep> [--dry-run]";
124: const OUTPUT_DIR = join(ROOT, "output");
125: const PREVIEW_COMMENT = join(OUTPUT_DIR, "preview-comment.md");
126: const GATEKEEPER_CONCURRENCY = 8;
127: // How many of the sweep's read-only API requests — one preview list per worker, one pull request per
128: // number — are in flight at once.
129: const API_CONCURRENCY = 8;

131: // Worker Previews are in private beta, and two of the features this script is built on are not in
132: // any released Wrangler: per-preview resource auto-provisioning (`previews.kv_namespaces` etc.
133: // declared binding-only), and `preview_id` on a `previews.services` entry, which is what points a
134: // preview at a *sibling* preview rather than at the baseline worker. Verified 2026-08-16 against
135: // the pinned 4.120.0 and the then-latest 4.123.0: both accept a binding-only KV entry in the
136: // schema but send `namespace_id: undefined`, and both silently drop `preview_id` from a service
137: // binding — which would leave the whole instance wired to the baselines. So the deploy runs on
138: // the draft build from https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/14416 instead, installed
139: // into a tmpdir. It pulls matching workers-sdk workspace packages from pkg.pr.new, hence the
140: // exotic-subdeps opt-out.
141: //
142: // Drop all of this — and set PREVIEW_WRANGLER=pnpm-exec-wrangler in the meantime to check — once
143: // both features ship: `preview_id` appearing in a released `config-schema.json` under
144: // `PreviewsConfig.properties.services.items.properties` is the signal.
145: const WRANGLER_PACKAGE = "https://pkg.pr.new/wrangler@14416";

147: function parseArgs(argv: string[]): { command: Command; dryRun: boolean } {
148:   const command = argv[0] as Command;
149:   if (!["config", "deploy", "delete", "sweep"].includes(command)) throw new Error(USAGE);
150:   const unknown = argv.slice(1).filter((arg) => arg !== "--dry-run");
151:   if (unknown.length > 0) throw new Error(`unknown argument: ${unknown[0]}\n${USAGE}`);
152:   return { command, dryRun: argv.includes("--dry-run") };
153: }
154: 
155: function runAsync(
156:   command: string,
157:   args: string[],
158:   options: { cwd?: string; env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv } = {},
159: ): Promise<void> {
160:   console.log(`running: ${command} ${args.join(" ")}`);
161:   return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
162:     const child = spawn(command, args, { env: process.env, stdio: "inherit", ...options });
163:     child.once("error", reject);
164:     child.once("close", (code) => {
165:       if (code === 0) resolve();
166:       else reject(new Error(`${command} ${args.join(" ")} failed with exit code ${code}`));
167:     });
168:   });
169: }
170: 
171: // Every item is attempted even after one fails
172: async function mapWithConcurrency<T, R>(
173:   items: readonly T[],
174:   concurrency: number,
175:   mapper: (item: T, index: number) => Promise<R>,
176: ): Promise<R[]> {
177:   const results: R[] = Array.from({ length: items.length });
178:   let nextIndex = 0;
179:   let firstError: unknown;
180: 
181:   async function worker() {
182:     while (nextIndex < items.length) {
183:       const index = nextIndex++;
184:       try {
185:         results[index] = await mapper(items[index], index);
186:       } catch (error) {
187:         if (firstError === undefined) firstError = error;
188:         else console.error(`Additional concurrent failure: ${describe(error)}`);
189:       }
190:     }
191:   }
192: 
193:   await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(concurrency, items.length) }, worker));
194:   if (firstError !== undefined) throw firstError;
195:   return results;
196: }
197: 
198: async function waitForAll(promises: readonly Promise<unknown>[]): Promise<void> {
199:   const results = await Promise.allSettled(promises);
200:   const failures = results.filter((r) => r.status === "rejected").map((r) => r.reason);
201:   for (const failure of failures.slice(1)) {
202:     console.error(`Additional concurrent failure: ${describe(failure)}`);
203:   }
204:   if (failures.length > 0) throw failures[0];
205: }

207: function describe(error: unknown): string {
208:   return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
209: }

211: // Codegen, the frontend bundle the router serves, and each gatekeeper's SPA bundle. Vite+ caches
212: // per task, so this is cheap on a warm tree.
213: //
214: // Whether the UI signs in through Cloudflare Access or with a password is a build-time flag
215: // (workshop-frontend/src/useAuth.ts), so a preview needs the same one build-release.mjs sets:
216: // otherwise it serves a password form the backend rejects every password from. The frontend's
217: // `build` task already declares `env: ['VITE_*']`.
218: function buildWorkspace(): Promise<void> {
219:   return runAsync("pnpm", ["run", "build"],
220:       { cwd: ROOT, env: { ...process.env, VITE_CF_ACCESS_MODE: "true" } });
221: }

223: function preparePreviewWrangler(): PreviewWrangler {
224:   const override = process.env.PREVIEW_WRANGLER;
225:   if (override) {
226:     return { command: override, ready: Promise.resolve(), cleanup: () => {} };
227:   }
228: 
229:   const installDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "preview-wrangler-"));
230:   try {
231:     writeFileSync(join(installDir, "package.json"), JSON.stringify({
232:       private: true,
233:       dependencies: { wrangler: WRANGLER_PACKAGE },
234:     }));
235:     writeFileSync(join(installDir, "pnpm-workspace.yaml"),
236:         "allowBuilds:\n  esbuild: true\n  sharp: true\n  workerd: true\n");
237:   } catch (error) {
238:     rmSync(installDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
239:     throw error;
240:   }
241: 
242:   return {
243:     command: join(installDir, "node_modules", ".bin", "wrangler"),
244:     ready: runAsync("pnpm",
245:         ["--config.blockExoticSubdeps=false", "--dir", installDir, "install"]),
246:     cleanup: () => rmSync(installDir, { recursive: true, force: true }),
247:   };

250: function readConfig(pkgDir: string): StagingConfig {
251:   return JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(pkgDir, STAGING_CONFIG_NAME), "utf8")) as StagingConfig;
252: }

254: // Wrangler's prose and its `code: 10007`, plus the `"code":10007` the Cloudflare API returns — the
255: // sweep lists previews over that API, and a worker whose baseline was never deployed has none.
256: function isMissingWorkerError(output: string): boolean {
257:   return /This Worker does not exist on your account|code"?:\s*10007/i.test(output);
258: }
259: 
260: // `wrangler --json` still logs informational text to stdout ahead of the JSON object, but the
261: // payload is emitted last.
262: function parseWranglerJson(raw: string): WranglerPreviewJson {
263:   const start = raw.lastIndexOf("\n{");
264:   const jsonStart = start >= 0 ? start + 1 : raw.indexOf("{");
265:   if (jsonStart >= 0) {
266:     const parsed = JSON.parse(raw.slice(jsonStart)) as WranglerPreviewJson;
267:     if (parsed.preview) return parsed;
268:   }
269:   throw new Error("Failed to parse wrangler JSON output: " +
270:       (jsonStart < 0 ? "no JSON payload found" : "no preview JSON payload found"));
271: }

273: function runWrangler(
274:   pkg: DeployablePackage,
275:   wranglerCommand: string,
276:   args: string[],
277:   // Written to the child's stdin, which is how secret values are handed over: argv is visible in
278:   // `ps` output and is echoed by the `running:` lines above every invocation.
279:   input?: string,
280: ): Promise<CommandResult> {
281:   return new Promise<CommandResult>((resolve, reject) => {
282:     const child = spawn(wranglerCommand, args, {
283:       cwd: pkg.dir,
284:       env: process.env,
285:       stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
286:     });
287:     // Closed immediately either way: no command here reads stdin except `secret bulk`, and an
288:     // empty pipe is the same EOF the previous `ignore` produced.
289:     child.stdin.end(input ?? "");
290:     let stdout = "";
291:     let stderr = "";
292:     child.stdout.setEncoding("utf8");
293:     child.stderr.setEncoding("utf8");
294:     child.stdout.on("data", (data: string) => { stdout += data; });
295:     child.stderr.on("data", (data: string) => { stderr += data; });
296:     child.once("error",
297:         (error) => reject(new Error(`Failed to run Wrangler for ${pkg.name}: ${error.message}`)));
298:     child.once("close", (status) => resolve({ status, stdout, stderr }));
299:   });
300: }

302: function writeCommandOutput(pkg: DeployablePackage, { stdout, stderr }: CommandResult): void {
303:   if (stdout) process.stdout.write(`[${pkg.name}]\n${stdout}`);
304:   if (stderr) process.stderr.write(`[${pkg.name}]\n${stderr}`);
305: }

307: // A Worker Preview is a branch of a baseline worker, so the baseline has to exist. Rather than
308: // requiring a separate bootstrap, deploy it the first time a preview reports it missing.
309: async function deployBaselineWorker(
310:   pkg: DeployablePackage,
311:   wranglerCommand: string,
312: ): Promise<void> {
313:   console.log(`baseline worker missing; running in ${pkg.name}: ` +
314:       `wrangler deploy -c ${STAGING_CONFIG_NAME}`);
315:   const result = await runWrangler(pkg, wranglerCommand, ["deploy", "-c", STAGING_CONFIG_NAME]);
316:   writeCommandOutput(pkg, result);
317:   if (result.status !== 0) {
318:     throw new Error(
319:         `wrangler deploy failed for baseline worker ${pkg.name} with exit code ${result.status}`);
320:   }
321: }

323: /**
324:  * Give a worker its secrets — the backend's admins and Cloudflare Access pair (see
325:  * backendSecrets). None of them is in the generated config, because Wrangler prints the values it
326:  * finds there and this workflow's logs are public; `secret bulk` prints only names and `********`,
327:  * and the values arrive on stdin rather than in argv.
328:  *
329:  * `preview secret bulk` writes the *Worker's Previews settings*, which every preview of that worker
330:  * inherits, so one upload covers every preview and each run refreshes them. The plain `secret bulk`
331:  * form is for the baseline worker itself, which is a real, publicly reachable instance and needs
332:  * the same Access application in front of it.
333:  */
334: async function uploadSecrets(
335:   pkg: DeployablePackage,
336:   wranglerCommand: string,
337:   secrets: Record<string, string>,
338:   { previews }: { previews: boolean },
339: ): Promise<CommandResult> {
340:   const args = [...previews ? ["preview"] : [], "secret", "bulk", "-c", STAGING_CONFIG_NAME];
341:   console.log(`running in ${pkg.name}: wrangler ${args.join(" ")} ` +
342:       `(${Object.keys(secrets).join(", ")} on stdin)`);
343:   const result = await runWrangler(pkg, wranglerCommand, args, JSON.stringify(secrets));
344:   writeCommandOutput(pkg, result);
345:   return result;
346: }

348: /**
349:  * Upload the backend's secrets, creating its baseline worker first if it does not exist yet.
350:  *
351:  * This runs before the backend's own preview rather than relying on deployPreview's self-heal,
352:  * because a worker has no Previews settings to write to until it exists — and a preview created
353:  * before the settings existed would come up with no admins and, worse, no Access application, so it
354:  * would fall back to password signup on a public URL.
355:  */
356: async function uploadBackendSecrets(
357:   backend: DeployablePackage,
358:   wranglerCommand: string,
359:   secrets: Record<string, string>,
360: ): Promise<void> {
361:   let result = await uploadSecrets(backend, wranglerCommand, secrets, { previews: true });
362:   if (result.status !== 0 && isMissingWorkerError(`${result.stdout}\n${result.stderr}`)) {
363:     await deployBaselineWorker(backend, wranglerCommand);
364:     // The baseline is briefly live without these, but it is only reachable through the *baseline*
365:     // router — which is deployed after it, in tier 3, on the same first run.
366:     const baseline = await uploadSecrets(backend, wranglerCommand, secrets, { previews: false });
367:     if (baseline.status !== 0) {
368:       throw new Error(`wrangler secret bulk failed for baseline worker ${backend.name} with exit ` +
369:           `code ${baseline.status}`);
370:     }
371:     result = await uploadSecrets(backend, wranglerCommand, secrets, { previews: true });
372:   }
373:   if (result.status !== 0) {
374:     throw new Error(`wrangler preview secret bulk failed for ${backend.name} with exit code ` +
375:         `${result.status}`);
376:   }
377: }

379: async function runPreviewCommand(

392: async function deployPreview(
393:   pkg: DeployablePackage,
394:   previewName: string,
395:   wranglerCommand: string,
396: ): Promise<DeployedPreview> {
397:   let result = await runPreviewCommand(pkg, previewName, wranglerCommand);
398:   if (result.status !== 0 && isMissingWorkerError(`${result.stdout}\n${result.stderr}`)) {
399:     await deployBaselineWorker(pkg, wranglerCommand);
400:     result = await runPreviewCommand(pkg, previewName, wranglerCommand);
401:   }
402:   if (result.status !== 0) {
403:     throw new Error(`wrangler preview failed for ${pkg.name} with exit code ${result.status}`);
404:   }

406:   const data = parseWranglerJson(result.stdout);
407:   // The id is what a sibling preview binds to, so it is required of every worker. A URL is not:
408:   // only the router sets `preview_urls`, and the other seventeen are reached over service
409:   // bindings alone.
410:   if (!data.preview?.id) throw new Error(`Wrangler did not emit a preview id for ${pkg.name}`);
411:   return {
412:     id: data.preview.id,
413:     slug: data.preview.slug ?? previewName,
414:     url: data.preview.urls?.[0],
415:     output: result.stdout,
416:   };
417: }

419: async function deletePreview(
420:   pkg: DeployablePackage,
421:   previewName: string,
422:   wranglerCommand: string,
423: ): Promise<void> {
424:   console.log(`running in ${pkg.name}: ` +
425:       `wrangler preview delete --name ${previewName} -c ${STAGING_CONFIG_NAME} -y`);
426:   const result = await runWrangler(pkg, wranglerCommand,
427:       ["preview", "delete", "--name", previewName, "-c", STAGING_CONFIG_NAME, "-y"]);
428:   writeCommandOutput(pkg, result);
429:   if (result.status === 0) return;
430: 
431:   // Deleting a preview that was never created — a PR closed before its first deploy finished, a
432:   // re-run of the cleanup job — is the expected case, not a failure.
433:   const output = `${result.stdout}\n${result.stderr}`;
434:   if (/not found|does not exist|10007|10025|10222/i.test(output)) {
435:     console.warn(`Preview ${previewName} for ${pkg.name} did not exist; continuing.`);
436:     return;
437:   }
438:   throw new Error(
439:       `wrangler preview delete failed for ${pkg.name} with exit code ${result.status}`);
440: }

442: /**
443:  * Delete one preview from every worker that carries it.
444:  *
445:  * Dependents first — the router, then the backend, then the rest concurrently — so nothing is left
446:  * bound to a preview that no longer exists.
447:  */
448: async function deletePreviewFrom(
449:   workers: readonly DeployablePackage[],
450:   previewName: string,
451:   wranglerCommand: string,
452: ): Promise<void> {
453:   const failures: unknown[] = [];
454:   const attempt = async (pkg: DeployablePackage) => {
455:     try {
456:       await deletePreview(pkg, previewName, wranglerCommand);
457:     } catch (error) {
458:       failures.push(error);
459:     }
460:   };
461: 
462:   const named = (name: string) => workers.filter((pkg) => pkg.name === name);
463:   for (const pkg of [...named("router"), ...named("workshop-backend")]) await attempt(pkg);
464:   await mapWithConcurrency(
465:       workers.filter((pkg) => !["router", "workshop-backend"].includes(pkg.name)),
466:       GATEKEEPER_CONCURRENCY, attempt);
467: 
468:   for (const failure of failures.slice(1)) {
469:     console.error(`Additional failure deleting ${previewName}: ${describe(failure)}`);
470:   }
471:   if (failures.length > 0) throw failures[0];
472: }

474: /**
475:  * Rewrite one package's `previews.services[].preview_id` from a map of **worker name** to preview
476:  * id, leaving entries the map doesn't mention alone (the router is patched twice — once for the
477:  * gatekeepers, once for the backend).
478:  */
479: function patchPreviewServiceBindings(
480:   pkg: DeployablePackage,
481:   previewIds: Record<string, string>,
482: ): void {
483:   const config = readConfig(pkg.dir);
484:   const services = config.previews?.services;
485:   if (!config.previews || !Array.isArray(services)) {
486:     throw new Error(`${pkg.name} preview config declares no service bindings to patch`);
487:   }
488: 
489:   const matched = new Set<string>();
490:   config.previews.services = services.map((service) => {
491:     if (!Object.hasOwn(previewIds, service.service)) return service;
492:     matched.add(service.service);
493:     return { ...service, preview_id: previewIds[service.service] };
494:   });
495: 
496:   // An unmatched key means the deployed worker's name and the name in the binding have drifted
497:   // apart. Left unchecked that is silent: the binding keeps no preview_id and resolves to the
498:   // baseline worker, so the instance comes up looking healthy and wired to the wrong code.
499:   const unmatched = Object.keys(previewIds).filter((name) => !matched.has(name));
500:   if (unmatched.length > 0) {
501:     throw new Error(`${pkg.name} has no service binding for ${unmatched.join(", ")}; its ` +
502:         `bindings name ${services.map((s) => s.service).join(", ")}`);
503:   }
504:   writePreviewConfig(pkg.dir, config);
505: }
506: 
507: // Only the router has a URL, and every BASE_URL in the instance was derived from that hostname
508: // before anything deployed — so a mismatch means the whole preview is misconfigured rather than
509: // merely oddly named. A worker with no `preview_urls` reports no URL at all, which is expected.
510: function assertRouterPreviewUrl(
511:   pkg: DeployablePackage,
512:   previewName: string,
513:   workersDevHost: string,
514:   actualUrl: string | undefined,
515: ): asserts actualUrl is string {
516:   const expected = previewUrlFor(pkg.name, previewName, workersDevHost);
517:   if (actualUrl !== expected) {
518:     throw new Error(
519:         `Expected preview URL ${expected} for ${pkg.name}, but Wrangler returned ${actualUrl}`);
520:   }
521: }
522: 
523: function assertNoPreviewUrl(pkg: DeployablePackage, actualUrl: string | undefined): void {
524:   if (actualUrl) {
525:     // Preview URLs are public. Only the router should be reachable directly, so one appearing on
526:     // a service-bound worker is a routing hole, not a cosmetic surprise.
527:     throw new Error(`${pkg.name} was given the public preview URL ${actualUrl}, but only the ` +
528:         "router should have one; check that its config still sets preview_urls: false");
529:   }
530: }

532: function writePreviewComment(
533:   baseUrl: string,
534:   slug: string,
535:   accountId: string | undefined,
536: ): void {
537:   const dashboardUrl = `https://dash.cloudflare.com/${accountId}/workers/services/view/` +
538:       `router/production/previews/${slug}`;

650: // --- sweep -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
651: //
652: // GitHub has no equivalent of GitLab's `environment.auto_stop_in`, and a PR that is force-closed,
653: // or whose cleanup job failed, leaves an instance behind — with an auto-provisioned KV pair and
654: // R2 bucket per preview, that leaks. This is the replacement, run nightly.
655: 
656: const PREVIEW_MAX_AGE_DAYS = 7;
657: 
658: async function cloudflareApi(path: string): Promise<unknown> {
659:   if (!process.env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) {
660:     throw new Error("CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is required to list previews");
661:   }
662:   const response = await fetch(`https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4${path}`, {
663:     headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN}` },
664:   });
665:   const body = await response.json().catch(() => ({})) as
666:       { success?: boolean; errors?: unknown; result?: unknown };
667:   if (!response.ok || body.success === false) {
668:     throw new Error(`Cloudflare API GET ${path} failed with ${response.status}: ` +
669:         JSON.stringify(body.errors ?? body));
670:   }
671:   return body.result;
