674: /**
675:  * One pull request's state.
676:  *
677:  * A 404 is an answer rather than a failure: the number was read out of a live preview's name, so a
678:  * pull request that does not exist means the preview outlived it. Anything else that goes wrong is
679:  * `unknown` — a transient 403 (GitHub's secondary rate limit) or 5xx must never be what deletes a
680:  * preview an open pull request is still using, so those fall back to being judged on age alone.
681:  */
682: async function fetchPullRequestState(repo: string, number: number): Promise<PullRequestState> {
683:   const path = `/repos/${repo}/pulls/${number}`;
684:   const headers: Record<string, string> = {
685:     Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
686:     "User-Agent": "cloudflare-os-preview-sweep",
687:   };
688:   if (process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN) headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN}`;
689: 
690:   try {
691:     const response = await fetch(`https://api.github.com${path}`, { headers });
692:     if (response.status === 404) return "missing";
693:     if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`GitHub API GET ${path} failed with ${response.status}`);
694:     const { state } = await response.json() as FetchedPullRequest;
695:     if (state === "open" || state === "closed") return state;
696:     throw new Error(`GitHub API GET ${path} reported the state ${JSON.stringify(state)}`);
697:   } catch (error) {
698:     console.warn(`${describe(error)}; pull request ${number}'s preview is swept on age alone.`);
699:     return "unknown";
700:   }
701: }
702: 
703: /**
704:  * Every listed preview's pull request state, keyed by preview name.
705:  *
706:  * The number is part of the name ({@link previewPullRequestNumber}), so this is one request per
707:  * *distinct* pull request — no walk of the repository's recent ones, and no bound on how old a pull
708:  * request the sweep can still recognize.
709:  */
710: async function pullRequestStates(
711:   repo: string,
712:   previewNames: readonly string[],
713: ): Promise<Map<string, PullRequestState>> {
714:   const numbers = [...new Set(previewNames
715:       .map((name) => previewPullRequestNumber(name))
716:       .filter((value): value is number => value !== undefined))];
717:   const states = await mapWithConcurrency(numbers, API_CONCURRENCY,
718:       (number) => fetchPullRequestState(repo, number));
719:   const byNumber = new Map(numbers.map((number, index) => [number, states[index]]));
720: 
721:   return new Map(previewNames.map((name) => {
722:     // A preview with no number in its name was deployed from a local checkout, and is something
723:     // this sweep can say nothing about: age alone decides it.
724:     const number = previewPullRequestNumber(name);
725:     return [name, (number === undefined ? undefined : byNumber.get(number)) ?? "unknown"];
726:   }));
727: }
728: 
729: function daysSince(timestamp: string): number {
730:   return (Date.now() - Date.parse(timestamp)) / 86_400_000;
731: }
732: 
733: function ageInDays(preview: ListedPreview): number | null {
734:   const stamp = preview.created_on ?? preview.created_at ?? preview.modified_on;
735:   const age = stamp ? daysSince(stamp) : NaN;
736:   return Number.isNaN(age) ? null : age;
737: }
738: 
739: /* Every preview live on any of this checkout's workers, as `name -> the workers carrying it` */
740: async function listPreviewsByName(
741:   accountId: string | undefined,
742:   packages: readonly DeployablePackage[],
743: ): Promise<Map<string, IndexedPreview>> {
744:   const lists = await mapWithConcurrency(packages, API_CONCURRENCY, async (pkg) => {
745:     let previews: unknown;
746:     try {
747:       previews = await cloudflareApi(
748:           `/accounts/${accountId}/workers/workers/${pkg.name}/previews`);
749:     } catch (error) {
750:       // A worker whose baseline has never been deployed on this account — one added since the last
751:       // preview ran — carries no previews rather than being a failure.
752:       if (!isMissingWorkerError(describe(error))) throw error;
753:       console.warn(`${pkg.name} does not exist on this account yet; it holds no previews.`);
754:       previews = [];
755:     }
756:     if (!Array.isArray(previews)) {
757:       throw new Error(`Expected a list of previews for ${pkg.name}, got ` +
758:           `${JSON.stringify(previews)?.slice(0, 200)}`);
759:     }
760:     return previews as ListedPreview[];
761:   });
762: 
763:   const index = new Map<string, IndexedPreview>();
764:   for (const [position, previews] of lists.entries()) {
765:     for (const preview of previews) {
766:       const age = ageInDays(preview);
767:       const found = index.get(preview.name);
768:       if (!found) {
769:         index.set(preview.name, { workers: [packages[position]], age });
770:         continue;
771:       }
772:       found.workers.push(packages[position]);
773:       // The newest copy decides the age, so a preview is only old enough to sweep once every
774:       // worker's copy of it is.
775:       if (age !== null && (found.age === null || age < found.age)) found.age = age;
776:     }
777:   }
778:   return index;
779: }
780: 
781: // Why this preview should go, or an empty list to keep it.
782: function staleReasons(preview: IndexedPreview, state: PullRequestState): string[] {
783:   const reasons: string[] = [];
784:   if (preview.age !== null && preview.age > PREVIEW_MAX_AGE_DAYS) {
785:     reasons.push(`${preview.age.toFixed(1)} days old`);
786:   }
787: 
788:   // `unknown` — a preview deployed by hand from a local checkout, or a GitHub request that failed —
789:   // contributes no reason of its own, leaving age to decide.
790:   if (state === "closed") reasons.push("its pull request is closed");
791:   else if (state === "missing") reasons.push("it names no pull request in this repository");
792:   return reasons;
793: }
794: 
795: async function sweep({ dryRun }: { dryRun: boolean }): Promise<void> {
796:   const { packages } = generatePreviewConfigs();
797:   const { router } = tiers(packages);
798:   const accountId = readConfig(router.dir).account_id;
799:   const repo = process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY;
800:   if (!repo) {
801:     console.warn("GITHUB_REPOSITORY is unset: sweeping on age only, not on PR state.");
802:   }
803: 
804:   const index = await listPreviewsByName(accountId, packages);
805:   console.log(`\n${index.size} preview(s) across ${packages.length} worker(s).`);
806:   const states = repo
807:       ? await pullRequestStates(repo, [...index.keys()])
808:       : new Map<string, PullRequestState>();
809: 
810:   const stale: { name: string; workers: DeployablePackage[]; reasons: string[] }[] = [];
811:   for (const [name, preview] of index) {
812:     const reasons = staleReasons(preview, states.get(name) ?? "unknown");
813:     if (reasons.length > 0) stale.push({ name, workers: preview.workers, reasons });
814:     else console.log(`  keeping ${name} (on ${preview.workers.map((pkg) => pkg.name).join(", ")})`);
815:   }
816: 
817:   if (stale.length === 0) {
818:     console.log("Nothing to sweep.");
819:     return;
820:   }
821:   for (const { name, workers, reasons } of stale) {
822:     console.log(`  ${dryRun ? "dry-run: would delete" : "deleting"} ${name} (${reasons.join(", ")}) ` +
823:         `from ${workers.map((pkg) => pkg.name).join(", ")}`);
824:   }
825:   if (dryRun) return;
826: 
827:   const wrangler = preparePreviewWrangler();
828:   const failed: string[] = [];
829:   try {
830:     await wrangler.ready;
831:     // Delete is keyed on `--name` alone; the generated configs only supply the worker and account
832:     // to target, so one set of them serves every preview name being swept.
833:     for (const { name, workers } of stale) {
834:       try {
835:         await deletePreviewFrom(workers, name, wrangler.command);
836:       } catch (error) {
837:         // Each preview is independent, and one left behind is a KV pair and an R2 bucket leaked
838:         // until tomorrow night, so the rest still go.
839:         failed.push(name);
840:         console.error(`Failed to delete ${name}: ${describe(error)}`);
841:       }
842:     }
843:   } finally {
844:     wrangler.cleanup();
845:   }
846:   console.log(`\nSwept ${stale.length - failed.length} of ${stale.length} preview(s).`);
847:   if (failed.length > 0) throw new Error(`failed to delete ${failed.join(", ")}`);
848: }
849: 
850: try {
851:   const args = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
852:   if (!existsSync(join(ROOT, "packages", "workshop-backend", "wrangler.jsonc"))) {
853:     throw new Error("run this from a full checkout: packages/workshop-backend is missing");

858:   else if (args.command === "delete") await remove(args);
859:   else await sweep(args);

185:       const out = execFileSync("git", argv,
186:           { cwd: ROOT, encoding: "utf8", stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "ignore"] }).trim();
187:       if (out) return argv[0] === "branch" ? out : `local-${out}`;
188:     } catch {
189:       // Not a git checkout, or a detached HEAD with no branch: try the next form.
190:     }
191:   }
192:   return "local-preview";
193: }
194: 
195: /**
196:  * The preview name, which is also the first label of its hostname — so CI passes the pull request's
197:  * number *and* its head branch, and a preview reads as `pr123-my-branch-router.<subdomain>`: still
198:  * recognizable, but unique per pull request. The number is what makes it unique, since two live
199:  * branches can slugify to one name (`feature/foo`, `feature-foo` and `Feature_Foo` all do) and would
200:  * otherwise share a single instance, overwriting each other and deleting each other on close.
201:  *
202:  * With no number — a local run — the name is the bare slug, and {@link previewPullRequestNumber}
203:  * reads none back out of it. The residual is that renaming a branch mid-review orphans the preview
204:  * deployed under the old name, until the nightly sweep collects it.
205:  */
206: export function resolvePreviewName(
207:   { name = process.env.PREVIEW_NAME, prNumber = process.env.PREVIEW_PR_NUMBER }:
208:       { name?: string; prNumber?: string } = {},
209: ): string {
210:   const ref = name || localRefName();
211:   // Anything that is not a number is treated as absent: on a scheduled run the workflow's
212:   // interpolation is the empty string, and no other value names a pull request.
213:   const pr = (prNumber ?? "").trim();
214:   if (!/^\d+$/.test(pr)) return slugifyPreviewName(ref);
215:   const prefix = `pr${pr}-`;
216:   return `${prefix}${slugifyPreviewName(ref, { reserve: prefix.length })}`;
217: }
218: 
219: export function previewPullRequestNumber(previewName: string): number | undefined {
220:   const match = /^pr(\d+)-/.exec(previewName);
221:   return match ? Number(match[1]) : undefined;
222: }
223: 
224: /**
225:  * The deployment admins seeded into the preview's ADMINS secret, from comma-separated
226:  * PREVIEW_ADMINS. These are Cloudflare Access identities — an email each, since that is what
227:  * {@link resolveAccess} makes the account name — so an entry that is not an email matches nobody.
228:  */
229: export function resolveAdmins(
230:   { list = process.env.PREVIEW_ADMINS }: { list?: string } = {},
231: ): string[] {
232:   const admins = (list ?? "").split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
233:   if (admins.length === 0) {
234:     console.warn("PREVIEW_ADMINS is unset: the preview will have no deployment admins, so the " +
235:         "/admin panel will be unreachable.");
236:   }
237:   return admins;
238: }

240: /**
241:  * Strip ids, names and other account-specific config from a resource binding list, leaving only
242:  * the binding name — which is how Wrangler is told to provision a fresh resource.
243:  */
244: function previewResourceBindings(resources: unknown): BindingDecl[] | undefined {
245:   if (!Array.isArray(resources)) return undefined;
246:   const bindings = (resources as { binding?: unknown }[])
247:       .map((resource) => ({ binding: resource.binding }))
248:       .filter((resource): resource is BindingDecl => typeof resource.binding === "string");
249:   return bindings.length > 0 ? bindings : undefined;
250: }
251: 
252: // The resource lists a baseline is given fresh rather than inheriting from the deployment its
253: // config was written for. All four hold `{ binding }`-shaped entries, which is what lets one loop
254: // do all of them.
255: const BASELINE_RESOURCE_KEYS = [
256:   "kv_namespaces", "r2_buckets", "d1_databases", "worker_loaders",
257: ] as const satisfies readonly (keyof StagingConfig)[];
258: 
259: /**
260:  * Do the same to the *baseline*, in place.
261:  *
262:  * The committed wrangler.jsonc files name resources for the deployment they were written for —
263:  * `bucket_name: "gadgets-blueprint-content"`, and KV entries carrying only a `preview_id`, which
264:  * is a local-dev Miniflare name rather than a namespace id. Passing those through would bind the
265:  * baseline to a bucket named for a different deployment, and would leave the KV bindings with no
266:  * id at all.
267:  *
268:  * A baseline exists here only so previews have something to branch from; nothing should ever
269:  * read its data. So it gets provisioned resources of its own, exactly as a preview does.
270:  */
271: function stripBaselineResources(config: StagingConfig): void {
272:   for (const key of BASELINE_RESOURCE_KEYS) {
273:     const stripped = previewResourceBindings(config[key]);
274:     if (stripped) config[key] = stripped;
275:   }
276: }
277: 
278: // Previews are throwaway, so invocation logs are worth their cost here even though production
279: // leaves them off.
280: function previewObservability(config: StagingConfig): ObservabilityConfig {
281:   return {
282:     ...config.observability,
283:     enabled: true,
284:     logs: { ...config.observability?.logs, invocation_logs: true },
285:   };
286: }
287: 
288: // How the backend calls gatekeepers: the GatekeeperVendor RPC entrypoint.
289: function backendGatekeeperServices(gatekeepers: string[], baseUrl: string): PreviewService[] {
290:   return gatekeepers.map((pkgName) => ({
291:     binding: gatekeeperBindingName(pkgName),
292:     service: pkgName,
293:     entrypoint: "GatekeeperVendor",
294:     // The Context gatekeeper namespaces each workshop's shared data by a "sharingDomain" carried
295:     // in its binding props (packages/gatekeeper-context/src/domain.ts). Using the preview's own
296:     // origin — as manifest-lib.ts does with $PUBLIC_BASE_URL — keeps each preview's collections
297:     // isolated from every other preview sharing the baseline gatekeeper.
298:     ...(pkgName === "gatekeeper-context" ? { props: { sharingDomain: baseUrl } } : {}),
299:   }));
300: }
301: 
302: // How the router calls gatekeepers: the default entrypoint, since it forwards whole HTTP
303: // requests rather than making vendor RPC calls.
304: function routerGatekeeperServices(gatekeepers: string[]): PreviewService[] {
305:   return gatekeepers.map((pkgName) => ({
306:     binding: gatekeeperBindingName(pkgName),
307:     service: pkgName,
308:   }));
309: }
310: 
311: function applyGatekeeper(
312:   pkgName: string,
313:   config: StagingConfig,
314:   { baseUrl }: PreviewContext,
315: ): void {
316:   config.vars = {
317:     ...config.vars,
318:     // Every gatekeeper is mounted under the router's origin, exactly as manifest-lib.ts
319:     // templates it for real instances ($PUBLIC_BASE_URL/gatekeeper/<short>).
320:     BASE_URL: `${baseUrl}/gatekeeper/${gatekeeperShortName(pkgName)}`,
321:   };
322:   config.previews = {
323:     observability: previewObservability(config),
324:     vars: { ...config.vars },
325:     ...(config.unsafe ? { unsafe: config.unsafe } : {}),
326:     ...(config.artifacts ? { artifacts: config.artifacts } : {}),
327:     ...(config.ai ? { ai: config.ai } : {}),
328:     ...(config.browser ? { browser: config.browser } : {}),
329:   };
330: 
331:   // KV namespaces and R2 buckets are auto-provisioned per preview: each preview gets its own,
332:   // and `wrangler preview delete` collects them.
333:   const kvNamespaces = previewResourceBindings(config.kv_namespaces);
334:   if (kvNamespaces) config.previews.kv_namespaces = kvNamespaces;
335:   const r2Buckets = previewResourceBindings(config.r2_buckets);
336:   if (r2Buckets) config.previews.r2_buckets = r2Buckets;
337: }
338: 
339: function applyBackend(
340:   config: StagingConfig,
341:   { baseUrl, gatekeepers }: PreviewContext,
342: ): void {
343:   // Injected rather than read from wrangler.jsonc, mirroring what manifest-lib.ts hardcodes for
344:   // every deployed backend (webFetch's toMarkdown conversion depends on it).
345:   config.ai = { binding: "WORKERS_AI" };
346:   config.services = backendGatekeeperServices(gatekeepers, baseUrl);
347:   // The origin is the only value the backend needs that is safe to write down here: ADMINS and the
348:   // Cloudflare Access pair are uploaded as *secrets* instead, out of band, because Wrangler prints
349:   // every plain-text var's value in its deploy summary and this workflow's logs are public. See
350:   // {@link backendSecrets} and preview.ts.
351:   config.vars = {
352:     ...config.vars,
353:     PUBLIC_BASE_URL: baseUrl,
354:   };
355:   config.previews = {
356:     observability: previewObservability(config),
357:     vars: { ...config.vars },
358:     ...(config.unsafe ? { unsafe: config.unsafe } : {}),
359:     // preview.ts patches each entry's preview_id once the gatekeeper previews exist.
360:     services: backendGatekeeperServices(gatekeepers, baseUrl),
361:     kv_namespaces: previewResourceBindings(config.kv_namespaces),
362:     r2_buckets: previewResourceBindings(config.r2_buckets),
363:     worker_loaders: previewResourceBindings(config.worker_loaders),
364:     ai: config.ai,
365:     ...(config.browser ? { browser: config.browser } : {}),
366:   };
367: }
368: 
369: function applyRouter(config: StagingConfig, { gatekeepers }: PreviewContext): void {
370:   // The one worker in the instance with a hostname: it is the origin, and everything else is
371:   // reached through it. See routerPreviewUrl.
372:   config.workers_dev = true;
373:   config.preview_urls = true;
374:   config.services = [
375:     { binding: "WORKSHOP_BACKEND", service: "workshop-backend" },
376:     ...routerGatekeeperServices(gatekeepers),
377:   ];
378:   config.previews = {
379:     observability: previewObservability(config),
380:     // Patched with preview_ids for the backend and every gatekeeper by preview.ts. Static
381:     // assets are not a `previews` key — the preview inherits the top-level `assets` stanza.
382:     services: structuredClone(config.services),
383:   };
384: }
385: 
386: /**
387:  * Build every package's preview config. Pure: `packages` is `[{ name, config }]` with `config`
388:  * the parsed wrangler.jsonc, and the result is a `Map` from package name to its preview config.
389:  */
390: export function buildPreviewConfigs({
391:   previewName,
392:   packages,
393:   accountId,
394:   workersDevHost,
395: }: {
396:   previewName: string;
397:   packages: readonly PackageConfig[];
398:   accountId: string;
399:   workersDevHost: string;
400: }): Map<string, StagingConfig> {
401:   if (!accountId || !workersDevHost) {
402:     throw new Error("buildPreviewConfigs needs both accountId and workersDevHost");
403:   }
404:   const baseUrl = routerPreviewUrl(previewName, workersDevHost);
405:   const gatekeepers = packages.map((pkg) => pkg.name).filter(isGatekeeperPackage).toSorted();
406:   const context: PreviewContext = { baseUrl, gatekeepers };
407:   const configs = new Map<string, StagingConfig>();
408: 
409:   for (const pkg of packages) {
410:     const config: StagingConfig = structuredClone(pkg.config);
411:     if (config.name !== pkg.name) {
412:       // Checked before the rename below, not after: every URL and service binding here is
413:       // derived from the package directory name, so a worker whose own name diverges from it
414:       // would be silently misconfigured rather than merely renamed.
415:       throw new Error(`${pkg.name}/wrangler.jsonc declares worker name "${config.name}"; the ` +
416:           `preview generator requires them to match`);
417:     }
418: 
419:     // `preview_urls` defaults to `workers_dev` when unset, but both are stated so a preview's
420:     // reachability never depends on a default changing, or on what the dashboard was last
421:     // toggled to — a deploy overwrites the dashboard value either way. applyRouter turns them
422:     // back on for the one worker that needs them.
423:     Object.assign(config, {
424:       name: pkg.name,
425:       account_id: accountId,
426:       workers_dev: false,
427:       preview_urls: false,
428:     });
429:     // The account has no zone here, and a preview cannot be served from one regardless.
430:     delete config.routes;
431:     stripBaselineResources(config);
432: 
433:     if (isGatekeeperPackage(pkg.name)) applyGatekeeper(pkg.name, config, context);
434:     else if (pkg.name === "workshop-backend") applyBackend(config, context);
435:     else if (pkg.name === "router") applyRouter(config, context);
436:     else throw new Error(`cannot build a preview config for package: ${pkg.name}`);
437: 
438:     configs.set(pkg.name, config);
439:   }
440: 
441:   assertBucketNamesFit(configs);
442:   return configs;
443: }
444: 
445: /**
446:  * Check {@link MAX_PREVIEW_NAME_LENGTH} against the workers and bindings that actually exist, so
447:  * a new worker with a longer name — or a longer binding on an existing one — fails here, naming
448:  * the number to lower, rather than at bucket creation halfway through a deploy.
449:  */
450: function assertBucketNamesFit(configs: Map<string, StagingConfig>): void {
451:   for (const [pkgName, config] of configs) {
452:     for (const { binding } of config.previews?.r2_buckets ?? []) {
453:       const suffix = binding.toLowerCase().replaceAll("_", "-");
454:       const length = `${config.name}-`.length + MAX_PREVIEW_NAME_LENGTH + `-${suffix}`.length;
455:       if (length <= R2_MAX_BUCKET_NAME_LENGTH) continue;
456:       throw new Error(`${pkgName}'s ${binding} bucket would be ${length} characters for a ` +
457:           `${MAX_PREVIEW_NAME_LENGTH}-character preview name, over R2's ` +
458:           `${R2_MAX_BUCKET_NAME_LENGTH}; lower MAX_PREVIEW_NAME_LENGTH to ` +
459:           `${MAX_PREVIEW_NAME_LENGTH - (length - R2_MAX_BUCKET_NAME_LENGTH)}`);
460:     }
461:   }
462: }
463: 
464: /**
465:  * The Cloudflare account previews deploy to, and its workers.dev subdomain.
466:  *
467:  * Neither has a default: this repository is public, so which account it deploys to is deployment
468:  * configuration rather than something to hardcode here, and a wrong-but-plausible default would
469:  * deploy somewhere unintended instead of failing. They are resolved together because every
470:  * gatekeeper's BASE_URL is derived from the host — setting one without the other would bake one
471:  * account's hostnames into another account's workers.
472:  *
473:  * The environment is read in the parameter defaults rather than the body so that
474:  * env-passthrough.test.ts, whose discovery is textual, can see both names.
475:  */
476: export function resolveTarget({
477:   accountId = process.env.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID,
478:   workersDevHost = process.env.PREVIEW_WORKERS_DEV_HOST,
479: }: { accountId?: string; workersDevHost?: string } = {}): {
480:   accountId: string;
481:   workersDevHost: string;
482: } {
483:   if (!accountId || !workersDevHost) {
484:     const missing = [
485:       ...(accountId ? [] : ["CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID"]),
486:       ...(workersDevHost ? [] : ["PREVIEW_WORKERS_DEV_HOST"]),
487:     ];
488:     throw new Error(`${missing.join(" and ")} must be set: together they name the Cloudflare ` +
489:         "account previews deploy to, and this repository deliberately hardcodes no default");
490:   }
491:   return { accountId, workersDevHost };
492: }
493: 
494: /** The Cloudflare Access application that authenticates a preview. */
495: export interface AccessConfig {
496:   /** The application's audience tag, matched as the JWT's `aud`. */
497:   aud: string;
498:   /** Team domain that issued the JWT, e.g. `https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com`. */
499:   iss: string;
500: }
501: 
502: /**
503:  * The Cloudflare Access application a preview sits behind.
504:  *
505:  * Required, like {@link resolveTarget}'s pair and for the same reasons. A preview is a public
506:  * workers.dev URL holding real gatekeeper capabilities, and an unset pair does not fail — the
507:  * backend can verify no assertion (access.ts) and quietly falls back to password signup — so this
508:  * fails closed rather than deploying an instance whose auth silently differs. The two move together
509:  * because verifying an assertion needs both, and either one alone verifies nothing.
510:  *
511:  * The environment is read in the parameter defaults rather than the body so that
512:  * env-passthrough.test.js, whose discovery is textual, can see both names.
513:  */
514: export function resolveAccess({
515:   aud = process.env.CF_ACCESS_AUD,
516:   iss = process.env.CF_ACCESS_ISS,
517: }: { aud?: string; iss?: string } = {}): AccessConfig {
518:   if (!aud || !iss) {
519:     const missing = [
520:       ...(aud ? [] : ["CF_ACCESS_AUD"]),
521:       ...(iss ? [] : ["CF_ACCESS_ISS"]),
522:     ];
523:     throw new Error(`${missing.join(" and ")} must be set: together they name the Cloudflare ` +
524:         "Access application that authenticates a preview, and a preview deployed without it " +
525:         "would fall back to password signup on a public URL");
526:   }
527:   return { aud, iss };
528: }
529: 
530: /**
531:  * The AI Gateway configuration, or nothing.
532:  *
533:  * Optional as a group, unlike {@link resolveAccess}: with CF_AI_GATEWAY unset a preview is BYOK,
534:  * exactly like a deployment that never configured a gateway, and the agent still works. Set, it
535:  * routes inference through Cloudflare AI Gateway with server-managed keys — and then the gateway
536:  * account is required, because `AiGatewayConfig` (ai-gateway.ts) throws without it. That throw
537:  * would otherwise land in a chat rather than in this deploy.
538:  *
539:  * The Run + Read token is not required with it. Every preview backend binds Workers AI (see
540:  * {@link applyBackend}), and the binding is the gateway transport whenever it is present: those
541:  * requests are pre-authenticated in-account, so neither inference nor a cost-log read needs a
542:  * token. Two configurations still do, and each is the deploy-time mirror of a constructor throw:
543:  * CF_AI_GATEWAY_USE_BINDING=false, which marks the gateway as living in a *different* account and
544:  * so forces the HTTPS transport, and the google provider, whose pi adapter refuses the binding's
545:  * fetch.
546:  *
547:  * The environment is read in the parameter defaults rather than the body so that
548:  * env-passthrough.test.js, whose discovery is textual, can see every name.
549:  */
550: export function resolveAiGateway({
551:   gateway = process.env.CF_AI_GATEWAY,
552:   accountId = process.env.CF_AI_GATEWAY_ACCOUNT_ID,
553:   apiToken = process.env.CF_AI_GATEWAY_API_TOKEN,
554:   providers = process.env.CF_AI_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS,
555:   useBinding: rawUseBinding = process.env.CF_AI_GATEWAY_USE_BINDING,
556: }: {
557:   gateway?: string;
558:   accountId?: string;
559:   apiToken?: string;
560:   providers?: string;
561:   useBinding?: string;
562: } = {}): Record<string, string> {
563:   // Normalized here rather than in the parameter default, which only runs when the caller omits
564:   // the value -- an explicitly passed " FALSE " would skip it and fail validation below.
565:   const useBinding = rawUseBinding?.trim().toLowerCase();
566:   const rest = { CF_AI_GATEWAY_ACCOUNT_ID: accountId, CF_AI_GATEWAY_API_TOKEN: apiToken,
567:     CF_AI_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS: providers, CF_AI_GATEWAY_USE_BINDING: useBinding };
568:   if (!gateway) {
569:     // Every one of these does nothing without a gateway name, so a set of them without it is a
570:     // half-finished configuration rather than a deliberate BYOK preview.
571:     const orphans = Object.entries(rest).filter(([, value]) => value).map(([name]) => name);
572:     if (orphans.length > 0) {
573:       console.warn(`CF_AI_GATEWAY is unset, so ${orphans.join(", ")} will be ignored: the preview ` +
574:           "will ask each user for their own model API keys.");
575:     }
576:     return {};
577:   }
578:   if (!accountId) {
579:     throw new Error("CF_AI_GATEWAY_ACCOUNT_ID must be set when CF_AI_GATEWAY is: the backend " +
580:         "cannot discover its own account, and refuses to start a chat without it");
581:   }
582:   if (useBinding !== undefined && useBinding !== "true" && useBinding !== "false") {
583:     // The backend compares against those two strings and treats anything else as unset, which for
584:     // an intended "false" is the opposite of what was asked for -- silently, and in a preview
585:     // nobody is reading the logs of.
586:     throw new Error(`CF_AI_GATEWAY_USE_BINDING must be "true" or "false", not ` +
587:         `"${rawUseBinding}": the backend reads any other value as unset.`);
588:   }
589:   // The two AiGatewayConfig throws the Workers AI binding does not cover. Raised here so a
590:   // half-configured preview fails its deploy rather than its first chat.
591:   if (!apiToken && useBinding === "false") {
592:     throw new Error("CF_AI_GATEWAY_API_TOKEN must be set when CF_AI_GATEWAY_USE_BINDING is " +
593:         "false: opting out of the binding leaves the HTTPS transport, which needs a Run + Read " +
594:         "token. Drop the opt-out unless the gateway is in another account.");
595:   }
596:   if (!apiToken && providers?.split(",").some(p => p.trim() === "google")) {
597:     throw new Error("CF_AI_GATEWAY_API_TOKEN must be set when the google provider is enabled: " +
598:         "pi's Google adapter refuses a custom fetch, so Google inference cannot ride the Workers " +
599:         "AI binding.");
600:   }
601:   return {
602:     CF_AI_GATEWAY: gateway,
603:     CF_AI_GATEWAY_ACCOUNT_ID: accountId,
604:     // Each of the three is optional on its own: no token rides the binding transport, no providers
605:     // means the gateway offers no server-keyed model, and no USE_BINDING takes the binding
606:     // whenever it is bound -- which, for a preview, is always.
607:     ...(apiToken ? { CF_AI_GATEWAY_API_TOKEN: apiToken } : {}),
608:     ...(providers ? { CF_AI_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS: providers } : {}),
609:     ...(useBinding ? { CF_AI_GATEWAY_USE_BINDING: useBinding } : {}),
610:   };
611: }

613: /**
614:  * The backend's secrets, keyed by the variable name it reads them as.
615:  *
616:  * These are deliberately *not* part of any generated config. Wrangler prints the value of every
617:  * plain-text var in its deploy summary (truncated to about forty characters) and every
618:  * `unsafe.bindings` entry verbatim in its configuration warning, and the preview workflow's logs
619:  * are public — so a maintainer's email, the audience tag and the team domain would all end up
620:  * there. GitHub's secret masking does not save them either: it replaces exact occurrences of a
621:  * registered secret, and what reaches the log is a reformatted, truncated slice of one. preview.ts
622:  * uploads these over stdin instead, with `wrangler preview secret bulk`, which prints names and
623:  * `********`.
624:  *
625:  * Setting the Access pair is also what closes the password path — the backend's `login()` and
626:  * `createAccount()` both throw once CF_ACCESS_AUD is set — so DISABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH is not needed.
627:  */
628: export function backendSecrets({
629:   admins = resolveAdmins(),
630:   access = resolveAccess(),
631:   aiGateway = resolveAiGateway(),
632: }: {
633:   admins?: string[];
634:   access?: AccessConfig;
635:   aiGateway?: Record<string, string>;
636: } = {}): Record<string, string> {
637:   return {
638:     // A secret is always text, so the array goes over as JSON. `#isAdmin()` already accepts that
639:     // form: ".env doesn't actually let you specify JSON bindings, so we also support a string that
640:     // parses as JSON array".
641:     ADMINS: JSON.stringify(admins),
642:     CF_ACCESS_AUD: access.aud,
643:     CF_ACCESS_ISS: access.iss,
644:     // The gateway name and its account are not secret in the way the token is, but they travel the
645:     // same way rather than as vars: one mechanism, and nothing about the deployment in the log.
646:     ...aiGateway,
647:   };
648: }

651: /** Write one package's generated preview config to its `wrangler.staging.jsonc`. */
652: export function writePreviewConfig(pkgDir: string, config: StagingConfig): void {
653:   writeFileSync(join(pkgDir, STAGING_CONFIG_NAME), JSON.stringify(config, null, 2) + "\n");

656: /**
657:  * Generate and write every package's preview config. Returns what the deploy/delete commands
658:  * need: the resolved preview name, the origin, and the packages in no particular order.
659:  */
660: export function generatePreviewConfigs(options: {
661:   previewName?: string;
662: } = {}): {
663:   previewName: string;
664:   workersDevHost: string;
665:   baseUrl: string;
666:   packages: DeployablePackage[];
667: } {
668:   const previewName = options.previewName ?? resolvePreviewName();
669:   const { accountId, workersDevHost } = resolveTarget();
670:   const packages = readDeployablePackages(PACKAGES_DIR);
671:   const configs = buildPreviewConfigs({
672:     previewName,
673:     packages,
674:     accountId,
675:     workersDevHost,
676:   });
677: 
678:   for (const pkg of packages) {
679:     const config = configs.get(pkg.name);
680:     if (!config) throw new Error(`no preview config was generated for ${pkg.name}`);
681:     writePreviewConfig(pkg.dir, config);
682:     console.log(`generated: ${join(pkg.dir, STAGING_CONFIG_NAME)}`);
683:   }

5: // points somewhere else. That is how a deployment ships its own formats: this repo is often a
6: // submodule, so a fork can't add files here without conflicting on every update -- it keeps its
7: // archives in its own tree and points the build at them. Whatever directory is named *is* the
8: // deployment's format set; it replaces this one rather than adding to it.
9: //
10: // Each blueprint is a `<name>.gadget` archive and a `<name>.json` beside it describing how to
11: // present it. Nothing references a list, so a directory outside this repo is self-contained.
12: //
13: // Archives are binary, so they are emitted as base64 -- the same "bundle a data file as a
14: // generated module" approach gatekeeper-context uses for its SPA.
15: 
16: import { readdir, readFile, writeFile, mkdir } from "node:fs/promises";
17: import { dirname, join, resolve, basename } from "node:path";
18: import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
19: 
20: const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
21: const pkgRoot = join(here, "..");
22: const sourceDir = resolve(pkgRoot, process.env.FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR ?? "format-blueprints");
23: const outFile = join(pkgRoot, "src", "generated", "format-blueprints.ts");
24: 
25: // Icons a blueprint may declare. Duplicated from the shared API's OUTPUT_ICONS because this script
26: // runs before (and without) a TypeScript build; the runtime validates against the real list, so
27: // the cost of drift is a build that rejects an icon the Worker would have accepted.
28: const OUTPUT_ICONS = ["fileText", "gridNine", "presentation", "appWindow", "flowArrow",
29:     "kanban", "chartBar", "table", "notebook", "listChecks"];
30: 
31: // Must match isReservedBlueprintKey() in src/blueprint-archive.ts. This build script runs without
32: // loading TypeScript modules, so keep the tiny control-key list here as well.
33: const RESERVED_BLUEPRINT_KEYS = new Set([".featured", ".adminConfig"]);
34: 
35: // Validated here rather than at runtime so a typo fails the build of whoever made it, instead of
36: // quietly presenting the wrong thing in production. Unknown keys are rejected too: silently
37: // ignoring one looks exactly like the field not working.
38: function parseSidecar(name, raw) {
39:   let bad = (message) => { throw new Error(`${name}.json: ${message}`); };
40:   let parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
41: 
42:   let string = (value, what) => {
43:     if (typeof value !== "string" || value.trim() === "") bad(`${what} must be a non-empty string`);
44:     return value;
45:   };
46: 
47:   let { blueprintId, title, description, output, author, revision, $comment, ...rest } = parsed;
48:   if (Object.keys(rest).length > 0) bad(`unknown keys: ${Object.keys(rest).join(", ")}`);
49: 
50:   if (!/^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/.test(blueprintId ?? "")) {
51:     bad("blueprintId must be a non-empty [a-zA-Z0-9._-] string");
52:   }
53:   if (RESERVED_BLUEPRINT_KEYS.has(blueprintId)) {
54:     bad(`blueprintId ${blueprintId} is reserved`);
55:   }
56:   if (typeof revision !== "number" || !Number.isInteger(revision) || revision < 1) {
57:     bad("revision must be a positive integer");
58:   }
59:   if (typeof output !== "object" || output === null) bad("output is required");
60:   let { id, noun, plural, icon, ...outputRest } = output;
61:   if (Object.keys(outputRest).length > 0) {
62:     bad(`unknown output keys: ${Object.keys(outputRest).join(", ")}`);
63:   }
64:   if (!OUTPUT_ICONS.includes(icon)) {
65:     bad(`output.icon must be one of: ${OUTPUT_ICONS.join(", ")}`);
66:   }
67:   if (typeof author !== "object" || author === null) bad("author is required");
68:   let { type: authorType, name: authorName, id: authorId, ...authorRest } = author;
69:   if (Object.keys(authorRest).length > 0) {
70:     bad(`unknown author keys: ${Object.keys(authorRest).join(", ")}`);
71:   }
72:   if (authorType !== undefined && authorType !== "user") bad(`author.type must be "user"`);
73: 
74:   return {
75:     blueprintId,
76:     title: string(title, "title"),
77:     description: string(description, "description"),
78:     output: {
79:       id: string(id, "output.id"),
80:       noun: string(noun, "output.noun"),
81:       plural: string(plural, "output.plural"),
82:       icon,
83:     },
84:     author: {
85:       type: "user",
86:       name: string(authorName, "author.name"),
87:       id: string(authorId, "author.id"),
88:     },
89:     revision,
90:   };
91: }
92: 
93: // An empty directory is a supported way to ship no formats, so it is a warning rather than an
94: // error. A mistyped FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR fails in readdir() above, which is the case worth
95: // catching.
96: let archives = (await readdir(sourceDir)).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".gadget")).toSorted();
97: if (archives.length === 0) {
98:   console.warn(`No *.gadget archives in ${sourceDir}; the deployment will bundle no formats.`);
99: }
100: 
101: let entries = [];
102: let totalBytes = 0;
103: let seen = new Map();
104: for (let file of archives) {
105:   let name = basename(file, ".gadget");
106:   let raw;
107:   try {
108:     raw = await readFile(join(sourceDir, `${name}.json`), "utf8");
109:   } catch (err) {
110:     if (err?.code !== "ENOENT") throw err;
111:     throw new Error(`${file} has no ${name}.json describing it.`, { cause: err });
112:   }
113: 
114:   let entry = parseSidecar(name, raw);
115:   // Two archives installing under one id would race, and only one would survive.
116:   let duplicate = seen.get(entry.blueprintId);
117:   if (duplicate) throw new Error(`${name}.json and ${duplicate}.json share id ${entry.blueprintId}`);
118:   seen.set(entry.blueprintId, name);
119: 
120:   let bytes = await readFile(join(sourceDir, file));
121:   totalBytes += bytes.byteLength;
122:   entries.push({ ...entry, archive: bytes.toString("base64") });
123: }
124: 
125: let generated = `// GENERATED by scripts/build-format-blueprints.mjs -- do not edit.
126: //
127: // The deployment's format blueprints, with their archives base64-encoded so they can be bundled
128: // into the Worker. Built from ${process.env.FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR ? "FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR" : "format-blueprints/"}.
129: 
130: import type { AiChatAuthorInfo, BlueprintOutput } from "@gadgets/workshop-shared/api";
131: 
132: // One bundled blueprint: how to present it, and the archive that says what it does. The build
133: // validates these sidecar fields; the archive itself is copied verbatim and checked when the
134: // importer writes it.
135: export type BundledFormatBlueprint = {
136:   blueprintId: string;
137:   title: string;
138:   description: string;
139:   output: BlueprintOutput;
140:   author: AiChatAuthorInfo;
141: 
142:   // Bumped when the archive changes, to trigger a reinstall on deployments already holding an
143:   // older copy. Everything else here is covered by the install fingerprint.
144:   revision: number;
145: 
146:   // The archive's bytes, base64-encoded.
147:   archive: string;
148: };
149: 
150: export const FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS: BundledFormatBlueprint[] = ${JSON.stringify(entries, null, 2)};
151: `;
152: 
153: // Skip the write when nothing changed. This script runs as a prerequisite of `build` and `test`,
154: // and rewriting an identical module would give it a fresh mtime, invalidating tsc's incremental
155: // cache for the whole package on every invocation. Same reason build-browser-runtime.mjs and the
156: // two SPA builds compare before writing.
157: let unchanged = false;
158: try {
159:   unchanged = await readFile(outFile, "utf8") === generated;
160: } catch (err) {
161:   if (err?.code !== "ENOENT") throw err;
162: }
163: 
164: if (unchanged) {
165:   console.log(`format blueprints up-to-date (${entries.length}): ${outFile}`);
166: } else {
167:   await mkdir(dirname(outFile), { recursive: true });
168:   await writeFile(outFile, generated);
169:   console.log(`Bundled ${entries.length} format blueprint(s) from ${sourceDir}, ` +
170:       `${(totalBytes / 1024).toFixed(0)} KiB raw -> ${outFile}`);
171: }

(End of file - total 171 lines)
</content>

display.text:
# Bundled format blueprints

This directory contains the output-format blueprints that ship with this repo, so a fresh deployment
can write a doc or build a deck without anyone having to build one first. A *format* is an ordinary
blueprint the deployment has promoted (see `AdminConfig.formats`); these are the ones it promotes out
of the box.

Each `.gadget` file here is committed **as data**. The first `/api` request a deployment serves
installs them into the BLUEPRINTS KV namespace and BLUEPRINT_CONTENT R2 bucket (see
`src/format-blueprints.ts`), after which they are ordinary blueprints. Nothing wakes on deploy, so a
fresh deployment is provisioned by its first visitor.

## Who owns what

A blueprint is two files with the same stem:

| | lives in | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the code, and the `bindings` it needs | `<name>.gadget` | what the blueprint *does* |
| `blueprintId`, title, description, `output` (noun/plural/icon), author, `revision` | `<name>.json` | what a human *curates*, so it's text in a reviewable file rather than fields inside a binary |

The installer writes the sidecar's values over whatever the archive happens to carry,
so an archive's own title and author are inert. The import script normalizes them anyway,
so the committed bytes don't contradict the sidecar.

## Changing a title, description or author

Edit the sidecar and rebuild. That's all — no archive rewrite, no `revision` bump: everything that
ends up in the installed metadata is part of the installed-version fingerprint (see
`formatBlueprintsManifestVersion`), so a reinstall follows on the next deploy.

## Updating a blueprint's code

Build it in a real Workshop, export it, and import the export:

```
pnpm import:format-blueprint ~/Downloads/Gadgets-Doc-v4.gadget format.document
```

That rewrites the archive, bumps `revision` in the sidecar, rebuilds
`src/generated/format-blueprints.ts`, and reports what it did:

```
Updated workspace-docs.gadget (format.document)
  code         23668 -> 24489 bytes (7c5413e5a482)
  bindings     (none)
  version      3 -> 4
  revision     2 -> 3  (workspace-docs.json)

  presented as "Workspace Docs" by Cloudflare, from workspace-docs.json
               [export called it "Gadgets Doc"]
```

The line worth reading is **`bindings`**, flagged `[CHANGED]` when the export needs something the old
copy didn't — an instantiating user will now be asked for it. `revision` is the reinstall trigger for
the one input the fingerprint can't see, the archive bytes; it's automated because forgetting it is
invisible (everything builds and deploys, and the old blueprint quietly stays put).

The script also round-trips the bytes it just wrote and checks the metadata and a content hash,
because these are committed as data and a corrupt archive would otherwise first surface when a
deployment tried to install it.

## Adding a new format

`--new` writes the sidecar for you, filling in what it can from the export:

```
pnpm import:format-blueprint ~/Downloads/Brief.gadget --new acme-brief
```

It then prints the handful of fields worth editing before you deploy — chiefly `output`, the noun,
plural and icon the sidecar owns rather than the archive, and `output.id`, the grouping key on the
Outputs page.
Make that one **generic** (`document`, not `acme-brief`): the Outputs page groups by it, so a
"Contract" blueprint declaring `document` is listed with the rest of the documents instead of
adding a filter chip of its own.

`blueprintId` defaults to the name you passed. It is the install key: reimporting the same id
updates that blueprint in place, and **changing it after a deployment has installed it** promotes
the new id as a *second* format while the old one stays in the New menu, updated by nothing.
Rename files freely; the id is the load-bearing part.


## Shipping your own formats

This directory is only the **default**. `FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR` points the build somewhere else:

```
FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR=../../acme-formats pnpm exec vp run build
```

`vp run`, not `pnpm build`: this package's `build` is a Vite+ task rather than a package.json
script, so pnpm cannot see it. `../vite.config.ts` explains why it has to be one.

Whatever directory it names *is* the deployment's format set — it replaces this one rather than
adding to it. Keep it in your own tree, in the same `<name>.gadget` + `<name>.json` layout; nothing
in it refers back to this repo. If you want one of ours too, copy the pair across once and own it
from then on.

This matters because this repo is usually a submodule: adding or deleting files *here* would
conflict on every update. Pointing the build at your own directory touches nothing, so the submodule
stays pristine forever. The import script honours the same variable, so you get the same workflow.

Two lighter options need no build change at all:

1. **Promote your own blueprints.** These are ordinary blueprints, and the standard set is admin
   curation (`AdminConfig.formats`). Publish a blueprint in your deployment and promote it in the
   admin Formats panel; disable the bundled ones you don't want. Nothing needs rebuilding, and this
   is the mechanism the bundled set is a convenience on top of, not a special case beside.
2. **Ship no formats.** Point `FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR` at an empty directory, and the deployment
   simply has none until an admin promotes something.

1: // Imports a `.gadget` archive exported from a running Workshop into the repo's bundled format
2: // blueprints.

6: // See format-blueprints/README.md for the workflow this belongs to.
7: //
8: // The archive is the blueprint's code; how it is presented lives in its `.json` sidecar, and the
9: // installer applies that over whatever the archive carries. So this script does not merge
10: // presentation -- it copies the code in, normalizes the archive's own now-inert metadata so the
11: // committed bytes don't contradict the sidecar, and bumps `revision` so deployments holding an
12: // older copy actually reinstall.
13: //
14: // Works on whichever directory the build uses (FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR), so a deployment maintaining
15: // its own formats gets the same workflow.
16: //
17: // It also reports the two things worth a human's attention: whether the export needs bindings the
18: // old copy didn't, and whether its title has drifted from the curated one.
19: 
20: import { readdir, readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
21: import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
22: import { basename, dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
23: import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
24: 
25: const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
26: const pkgRoot = join(here, "..");
27: const sourceDir = resolve(pkgRoot, process.env.FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR ?? "format-blueprints");
28: 
29: // See src/blueprint-archive.ts, which is the authority on this format: a 24-byte prefix (magic,
30: // version, metadata byte length, content byte length), UTF-8 JSON metadata, gzipped Yjs snapshot.
31: // Re-implemented here because this runs as a plain node script outside the Worker.
32: const MAGIC = 0xec2e2d3a2300e317n;
33: const VERSION = 1;
34: const PREFIX_BYTES = 24;
35: 
36: function fail(message) {
37:   console.error(`error: ${message}`);
38:   process.exit(1);
39: }
40: 
41: function parseArchive(bytes, label) {
42:   if (bytes.byteLength < PREFIX_BYTES) fail(`${label}: too short to be a .gadget archive`);
43:   const view = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, bytes.byteLength);
44:   if (view.getBigUint64(0) !== MAGIC) fail(`${label}: not a .gadget archive (bad magic)`);
45:   const version = view.getUint32(8);
46:   if (version !== VERSION) fail(`${label}: unsupported archive version ${version}`);
47:   const metadataLength = view.getUint32(12);
48:   const contentLength = Number(view.getBigUint64(16));
49:   const content = bytes.subarray(PREFIX_BYTES + metadataLength);
50:   if (content.byteLength !== contentLength) {
51:     fail(`${label}: content is ${content.byteLength} bytes, prefix claims ${contentLength}`);
52:   }
53:   let metadata;
54:   try {
55:     metadata = JSON.parse(
56:         new TextDecoder().decode(bytes.subarray(PREFIX_BYTES, PREFIX_BYTES + metadataLength)));
57:   } catch (err) {
58:     fail(`${label}: metadata is not valid JSON (${err.message})`);
59:   }
60:   return { metadata, content };
61: }
62: 
63: function serializeArchive(metadata, content) {
64:   const metadataBytes = new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(metadata));
65:   const out = new Uint8Array(PREFIX_BYTES + metadataBytes.byteLength + content.byteLength);
66:   const view = new DataView(out.buffer);
67:   view.setBigUint64(0, MAGIC);
68:   view.setUint32(8, VERSION);
69:   view.setUint32(12, metadataBytes.byteLength);
70:   view.setBigUint64(16, BigInt(content.byteLength));
71:   out.set(metadataBytes, PREFIX_BYTES);
72:   out.set(content, PREFIX_BYTES + metadataBytes.byteLength);
73:   return out;
74: }
75: 
76: const sha = (bytes) => createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex").slice(0, 12);
77: 
78: // --- Arguments -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
79: 
80: // Every sidecar in the directory, so a blueprintId can be resolved to the files that hold it.
81: const sidecars = [];
82: for (const file of (await readdir(sourceDir)).filter(f => f.endsWith(".json")).toSorted()) {
83:   const name = basename(file, ".json");
84:   const source = await readFile(join(sourceDir, file), "utf8");
85:   sidecars.push({ name, source, ...JSON.parse(source) });
86: }
87: 
88: const args = process.argv.slice(2);
89: const newAt = args.indexOf("--new");
90: const newName = newAt === -1 ? undefined : args.splice(newAt, 2)[1];
91: const [archivePath, blueprintId] = args;
92: 
93: if (!archivePath || (!blueprintId && !newName)) {
94:   console.error("usage: pnpm import:format-blueprint <export.gadget> <blueprintId>");
95:   console.error("       pnpm import:format-blueprint <export.gadget> --new <name>");
96:   console.error("");
97:   console.error(`formats in ${sourceDir}:`);
98:   for (const entry of sidecars) {
99:     console.error(`  ${entry.blueprintId.padEnd(20)} ${entry.name}.gadget`);
100:   }
101:   process.exit(2);
102: }
103: 
104: if (newName && !/^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/.test(newName)) {
105:   fail(`--new ${newName}: name must be [a-zA-Z0-9._-]`);
106: }
107: if (newName && sidecars.some(e => e.name === newName)) {
108:   fail(`${newName}.json already exists; import into it by blueprintId instead`);
109: }
110: 
111: const entry = newName
112:     ? { name: newName, scaffold: true }
113:     : sidecars.find(e => e.blueprintId === blueprintId);
114: if (!entry) {
115:   fail(`no sidecar declares blueprintId "${blueprintId}".\n` +
116:        `       Use --new <name> to start one.`);
117: }
118: const targetPath = join(sourceDir, `${entry.name}.gadget`);
119: const sidecarPath = join(sourceDir, `${entry.name}.json`);
120: 
121: // --- Read ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
122: 
123: // Nothing is written before this point, so a bad argument leaves the repo untouched.
124: let incomingBytes;
125: try {
126:   incomingBytes = await readFile(resolve(archivePath));
127: } catch (err) {
128:   fail(err?.code === "ENOENT" ? `no such file: ${archivePath}` : `${archivePath}: ${err.message}`);
129: }
130: const incoming = parseArchive(incomingBytes, archivePath);
131: 
132: let existing;
133: try {
134:   existing = parseArchive(await readFile(targetPath), `${entry.name}.gadget`);
135: } catch (err) {
136:   if (err?.code !== "ENOENT") throw err;
137: }
138: 
139: // --- Scaffold ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
140: 
141: let scaffoldSidecar;
142: 
143: // `--new` writes the sidecar so nobody has to learn its shape from the README. Everything it can
144: // take from the export it does; what is left is prose and the `output` vocabulary, which the
145: // sidecar owns even when the export carries one (see the dropped keys below). The values it guesses
146: // are valid, so the import completes and the format works -- the TODO list printed at the end is
147: // what makes them worth revisiting.
148: if (entry.scaffold) {
149:   // Borrowed from a sibling if there is one: a directory's blueprints are published by the same
150:   // people, and the export's author is whoever happened to build it in a Workshop.
151:   const author = sidecars[0]?.author ?? incoming.metadata.author;
152:   const title = incoming.metadata.title || entry.name;
153: 
154:   Object.assign(entry, {
155:     blueprintId: entry.name,
156:     title,
157:     description: incoming.metadata.description || `TODO: say what a ${title} is for.`,
158:     output: { id: entry.name, noun: title, plural: `${title}s`, icon: "appWindow" },
159:     author,
160:     revision: 1,
161:   });
162: 
163:   // Held rather than written, so that a scaffold whose archive turns out to be unusable doesn't
164:   // leave a sidecar behind with nothing beside it. Written with the archive below.
165:   scaffoldSidecar = `${JSON.stringify({
166:     blueprintId: entry.blueprintId,
167:     title: entry.title,
168:     description: entry.description,
169:     output: entry.output,
170:     author: entry.author,
171:     revision: entry.revision,
172:   }, null, 2)}\n`;
173: }
174: 
175: // --- Write -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
176: 
177: // The archive's own presentation is inert -- the installer takes those fields from the sidecar --
178: // but committed bytes that say something different are misleading, and would surface if anyone
179: // imported this file by hand through the UI. So they are normalized to the sidecar's values. The
180: // rest is the export's: `bindings` because it is part of what the blueprint does, and the dates
181: // because they are real provenance from the workspace this came from.
182: //
183: // `version` is the blueprint's own version, used as its R2 content key, and comes from the export:
184: // the authoring workspace already increments it every time the blueprint is republished.
185: const metadata = {
186:   title: entry.title,
187:   description: entry.description,
188:   author: entry.author,
189:   created: incoming.metadata.created,
190:   version: incoming.metadata.version,
191:   lastUpdated: incoming.metadata.lastUpdated,
192:   bindings: incoming.metadata.bindings ?? {},
193: };
194: 
195: // `output` is declared in the sidecar and `screenshot` refers to bytes stored outside the archive,
196: // so neither belongs in a bundled copy: one would be a second source of truth that silently loses,
197: // the other a dangling reference.
198: const dropped = ["output", "screenshot"].filter((key) => key in incoming.metadata);
199: 
200: const archiveBytes = serializeArchive(metadata, incoming.content);
201: 
202: // Round-trip before writing anything, rather than trusting the serializer: these bytes are
203: // committed as data, and a corrupt archive would otherwise first surface when a deployment tried
204: // to install it.
205: const written = parseArchive(archiveBytes, `${entry.name}.gadget`);
206: if (JSON.stringify(written.metadata) !== JSON.stringify(metadata)) {
207:   fail(`${entry.name}.gadget: metadata did not survive the round trip`);
208: }
209: if (sha(written.content) !== sha(incoming.content)) {
210:   fail(`${entry.name}.gadget: content did not survive the round trip`);
211: }
212: 
213: // The reinstall trigger for deployments that already hold an older copy. Automated because it is
214: // both the easiest step to forget and the one whose failure is invisible: everything builds and
215: // deploys, and the old blueprint quietly stays put. (Presentation changes need no bump -- they are
216: // part of the installed-version fingerprint. Archive bytes aren't, which is what this is for. A
217: // blueprint being scaffolded has nothing to reinstall over, so it keeps the revision 1 it was
218: // written with.)
219: //
220: // Edited as text rather than re-serialized so the sidecar keeps its formatting and any $comment.
221: let bumpedSidecar;
222: if (!entry.scaffold) {
223:   bumpedSidecar = entry.source.replace(/"revision":\s*\d+/, `"revision": ${entry.revision + 1}`);
224:   if (bumpedSidecar === entry.source) fail(`${entry.name}.json has no revision to bump`);
225: }
226: 
227: // Everything that can fail has failed by now: the sidecar's new contents are computed above, so
228: // the archive can't land carrying an old revision -- deployments holding the previous copy would
229: // never reinstall, which is the exact silent failure the bump exists to prevent. The two writes
230: // are still sequential, so an I/O error between them leaves the archive updated and the sidecar
231: // not; re-running the import fixes that.
232: await writeFile(targetPath, archiveBytes);
233: if (bumpedSidecar ?? scaffoldSidecar) await writeFile(sidecarPath, bumpedSidecar ?? scaffoldSidecar);
234: 
235: // --- Report ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
236: 
237: const oldBindings = Object.keys(existing?.metadata.bindings ?? {}).toSorted().join(",");
238: const newBindings = Object.keys(metadata.bindings).toSorted().join(",");
239: const contentUnchanged = existing && sha(existing.content) === sha(incoming.content);
240: 
241: console.log(`${existing ? "Updated" : "Imported"} ${entry.name}.gadget (${entry.blueprintId})`);
242: console.log(`  code         ${existing ? `${existing.content.byteLength} -> ` : ""}` +
243:     `${incoming.content.byteLength} bytes (${sha(incoming.content)})` +
244:     `${contentUnchanged ? "   [unchanged]" : ""}`);
245: console.log(`  bindings     ${newBindings || "(none)"}` +
246:     `${oldBindings !== newBindings ? `   [CHANGED from ${oldBindings || "(none)"}]` : ""}`);
247: console.log(`  version      ${existing ? `${existing.metadata.version} -> ` : ""}${metadata.version}`);
248: console.log(`  revision     ${entry.scaffold ? "1  (new)"
249:     : `${entry.revision} -> ${entry.revision + 1}  (${entry.name}.json)`}`);
250: console.log("");
251: console.log(`  presented as "${metadata.title}" by ${metadata.author.name}, from ${entry.name}.json` +
252:     `${incoming.metadata.title !== metadata.title
253:         ? `\n               [export called it "${incoming.metadata.title}"]` : ""}`);
254: if (dropped.length > 0) {
255:   console.log(`  dropped      ${dropped.join(", ")}   [owned by the sidecar / stored separately]`);
256: }
257: 
258: // The scaffold guessed these, and a guess that works is the kind nobody revisits.
259: if (entry.scaffold) {
260:   console.log("");
261:   console.log(`  Wrote ${entry.name}.json. Edit before deploying:`);
262:   console.log(`    blueprintId  "${entry.blueprintId}" -- the install key, and fixed once deployed`);
263:   console.log(`    output.id    "${entry.output.id}" -- groups it on the Outputs page, so prefer a`);
264:   console.log(`                 generic word ("document") over this blueprint's own name`);
265:   console.log(`    output       noun "${entry.output.noun}", plural "${entry.output.plural}", ` +
266:       `icon "${entry.output.icon}"`);
267:   console.log(`    description  what the format is *for* -- the agent reads it to decide when to`);
268:   console.log(`                 use this format`);
269: }
270: console.log("");
271: await import("./build-format-blueprints.mjs");

3:  * package's `vite.config.ts`. Plain objects rather than `defineConfig`, so the packages need no
4:  * resolvable `vite-plus` import of their own -- the same reason

6:  * copies of Vite+'s rather than imports of them, which is what keeps that true.
7:  *
8:  * TypeScript, unlike the `.mjs`/`.js` around it in this directory, because nothing here is ever run
9:  * by `node` -- both modules are imported only from `vite.config.ts` files, which vite bundles -- and
10:  * being TS means a malformed task or a mistyped `base` is a compile error rather than a glob that
11:  * silently never matches. Importers still write the `.js` extension in the specifier; TS and vite
12:  * both resolve it to the `.ts`.
13:  *
14:  * `test` is a task rather than a package.json script so the scratch paths every `vitest run` writes
15:  * and then reads back can be kept out of the fingerprint: vp declines to cache a task that reads a
16:  * path it also wrote, and without these exclusions almost nothing cached. vp forbids a task and a
17:  * script sharing a name, so the packages have no `test` script any more and
18:  * `vp run -F <package> test` is what replaces `pnpm --filter <package> test`.
19:  */
20: 
21: /** A glob paired with the directory its pattern resolves against. */
22: export type GlobWithBase = {
23:   pattern: string
24:   base: 'package' | 'workspace'
25: }
26: 
27: /** The subset of a Vite+ task this factory produces. */
28: export type VitestTask = {
29:   command: string | string[]
30:   input: (GlobWithBase | { auto: boolean })[]
31:   output: (GlobWithBase | { auto: boolean })[]
32: }
33: 
34: /** A Vite+ config carrying a `run.tasks` map. */
35: export type RunTasksConfig = {
36:   run?: {
37:     tasks?: Record<string, unknown>
38:   }
39: }
40: 
41: /**
42:  * Paths vitest generates and reads back on the next run, excluded from both the fingerprint and the
43:  * archived outputs:
44:  *
45:  * - `node_modules/.vite/vitest/<project-hash>/results.json` -- per-file durations and pass/fail,
46:  *   read by vitest's `BaseSequencer` to order failed-first and slowest-first. Distinct from the
47:  *   sibling `node_modules/.vite/deps`, which is a real transform cache.
48:  * - `node_modules/.vite-temp/*.config.ts.timestamp-*.mjs` -- vite's default `bundle` config loader
49:  *   compiles a TS config to a temp module here, imports it, then unlinks it. The name carries a
50:  *   timestamp, so every run writes a fresh path and no run could ever match a previous fingerprint.
51:  * - `.wrangler/validate/**` -- the capnweb-validate build tree, regenerated and then loaded by any
52:  *   suite that starts a worker under `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`. It is derived from sources
53:  *   that are tracked, so dropping it from the fingerprint loses no invalidation. `build:app`
54:  *   excludes the same tree, for the same reason.
55:  *
56:  * These are tool-managed scratch paths that Vite+'s own cooperative tracking already excludes for
57:  * `vp build` (`guide/automatic-data-tracking.md` names `node_modules/.vite-temp` as a path that
58:  * "should not be inputs or outputs"), so excluding them is the blessed shape rather than a
59:  * workaround.
60:  *
61:  * Workspace-wide rather than package-relative: tracking reaches past the package that owns the
62:  * task, so a sibling's scratch files would otherwise stay in this package's fingerprint and the
63:  * packages would invalidate each other -- the same trap documented on `build:app`.
64:  *
65:  * This list is unlikely to be closed. When a test task stops caching, `vp run --last-details` names
66:  * the path it read and wrote -- add it here if it is shared, or at the call site if it is one
67:  * package's own (as `workshop-frontend`'s `dist/**` is).
68:  */
69: const VITEST_SCRATCH_EXCLUSIONS: GlobWithBase[] = [
70:   { pattern: '!**/node_modules/.vite/**', base: 'workspace' },
71:   { pattern: '!**/node_modules/.vite-temp/**', base: 'workspace' },
72:   { pattern: '!**/.wrangler/**', base: 'workspace' },
73: ]
74: 
75: /**
76:  * Seconds of silence after which a command is considered wedged. A healthy `vitest run` prints a
77:  * line per completed test file, so silence -- not wall clock -- is what distinguishes a hang from a
78:  * slow suite.
79:  */
80: const IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 60
81: 
82: /** Wall-clock backstop, for a command that stays chatty while looping forever. */
83: const TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 600
84: 
85: /**
86:  * Nothing under vitest bounds a wedged run -- its own timeouts are enforced inside the test worker
87:  * that died, and Vite+ has no task timeout -- so a hung suite stalls the whole `vp run` until
88:  * something outside kills it

90:  * The path must stay *relative*: the command string is part of the cache fingerprint, so an
91:  * absolute path derived from `import.meta.url` would differ per checkout and per CI runner and
92:  * destroy cache portability. Relative works because every consumer lives at `packages/<name>/`.
93:  *
94:  * The thresholds are baked into the string rather than read from the environment for the same
95:  * reason: a cached `vp` run strips undeclared env vars, so an override would silently not apply
96:  * (and would owe `scripts/env-passthrough.test.ts` an entry). Here a policy change is a visible,
97:  * fingerprinted change.
98:  */
99: export const withTestTimeout = (command: string): string =>
100:   `node ../../scripts/with-timeout.ts` +
101:   ` --idle ${IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS} --max ${TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS} -- ${command}`
102: 
103: /**
104:  * The `test` task for a package, given the vitest invocation its `test` script used to hold.
105:  * An array of commands is run in order and cached as one entry per command, so a package with
106:  * codegen ahead of its tests can still replay the codegen and re-run only the tests.
107:  *
108:  * `extraExclusions` adds package-specific patterns to the shared ones. Only `workshop-frontend`
109:  * needs any: nothing else here writes a build artifact into a directory its own tests track.
110:  *
111:  * Every command is wrapped in the watchdog above, including the codegen steps some packages bundle
112:  * into this task (`workshop-backend`'s `node build-browser-runtime.mjs`) -- those are equally
113:  * unbounded.
114:  */
115: export function vitestTask(
116:   command: string | string[],
117:   extraExclusions: GlobWithBase[] = [],
118: ): VitestTask {
119:   const exclusions = [...VITEST_SCRATCH_EXCLUSIONS, ...extraExclusions]
120:   return {
121:     command: Array.isArray(command) ? command.map(withTestTimeout) : withTestTimeout(command),
122:     input: [{ auto: true }, ...exclusions],
123:     output: [{ auto: true }, ...exclusions],
124:   }
125: }
126: 
127: /**
128:  * A whole `vite.config.ts` default export, for the packages that need no other Vite+ settings.
129:  * Packages that do use `withVitestTask()` or `vitestTask()` instead.
130:  */
131: export default function vitestTaskViteConfig(
132:   command: string | string[],
133:   extraExclusions: GlobWithBase[] = [],
134: ): { run: { tasks: { test: VitestTask } } } {
135:   return {
136:     run: {
137:       tasks: {
138:         test: vitestTask(command, extraExclusions),
139:       },
140:     },
141:   }
142: }
143: 
144: /**
145:  * `config` with the `test` task added to whatever tasks it already declares. Used by
146:  * `gatekeeper-configurator-vite-config.ts` to build its `withTests` variant.
147:  */
148: export function withVitestTask<T extends RunTasksConfig>(
149:   config: T,
150:   command: string | string[],
151: ): T & { run: { tasks: Record<string, unknown> } } {
152:   return {
153:     ...config,
154:     run: {
155:       ...config.run,
156:       tasks: {
157:         ...config.run?.tasks,
158:         test: vitestTask(command),
159:       },
160:     },
161:   }
162: }

<content>
1: // Run a command under two watchdogs -- an idle timer on its output and a total wall-clock cap --
2: // and kill its whole process tree when either fires.
3: //
4: //     node ../../scripts/with-timeout.ts --idle <secs> --max <secs> -- <command> [args...]
5: //
6: // It exists because nothing else in the test stack bounds a wedged run. Vite+ has no task timeout
7: // (`vp run --help` offers only concurrency flags, and `timeout` appears nowhere in its docs), and
8: // vitest's `testTimeout`/`hookTimeout` are enforced *inside* the test worker, so they die with it;
9: // the one process-level watchdog, `teardownTimeout`, is armed after the run resolves and therefore
10: // never arms when the run is what hangs. Underneath that,
11: // `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` imports Miniflare without passing `onWorkerdCrashRestart`, so a
12: // workerd that dies mid-run leaves the pool awaiting a reply that will never arrive. The result is
13: // an unbounded local hang, and in CI an anonymous job-level kill that names no culprit.
14: //
15: // Silence is the primary detector rather than wall-clock: a healthy `vitest run` prints a line per
16: // completed test file, and a wedged one goes quiet. The total cap is the backstop for a command
17: // that stays chatty while looping forever.
18: //
19: // Exit codes: 124 when a threshold fired (GNU `timeout`'s, and distinct from any vitest code), the
20: // child's own code otherwise, or `128 + signal` when the child or this wrapper was signalled.
21: 
22: import { execFile, spawn } from "node:child_process";
23: import { constants } from "node:os";
24: import { resolveBinEntry } from "./bin-entry.ts";
25: import { collectTree, killProcessTreeEscalating } from "./kill-process-tree.ts";
26: 
27: /** Exit status for a threshold firing, matching GNU `timeout`. */
28: const TIMED_OUT_EXIT_CODE = 124;
29: 
30: /** How long a signalled tree gets to exit on its own before the SIGKILL. */
31: const KILL_GRACE_MS = 5_000;
32: 
33: const USAGE = "usage: with-timeout.ts --idle <secs> --max <secs> -- <command> [args...]";
34: 
35: type Options = {
36:   idleMs: number;
37:   maxMs: number;
38:   argv: string[];
39: };
40: 
41: // Both thresholds are required rather than defaulted: the numbers are policy, and a caller that
42: // forgot one should not silently get a different bound than it asked for. Fractional seconds are
43: // accepted so the tests can drive this with sub-second thresholds.
44: function parseArgs(args: string[]): Options {
45:   let idleMs: number | undefined;
46:   let maxMs: number | undefined;
47:   let index = 0;
48:   for (; index < args.length; index++) {
49:     const flag = args[index];
50:     if (flag === "--") {
51:       index++;
52:       break;
53:     }
54:     const value = args[++index];
55:     if (flag === "--idle") idleMs = parseSeconds(flag, value);
56:     else if (flag === "--max") maxMs = parseSeconds(flag, value);
57:     else fail(`unknown option ${flag}\n${USAGE}`);
58:   }
59:   const argv = args.slice(index);
60:   if (idleMs === undefined || maxMs === undefined) fail(`--idle and --max are both required\n${USAGE}`);
61:   if (argv.length === 0) fail(`no command given\n${USAGE}`);
62:   return { idleMs, maxMs, argv };
63: }
64: 
65: function parseSeconds(flag: string, value: string | undefined): number {
66:   const seconds = Number(value);
67:   if (!Number.isFinite(seconds) || seconds <= 0) fail(`${flag} needs a positive number of seconds`);
68:   return seconds * 1000;
69: }
70: 
71: function fail(message: string): never {
72:   process.stderr.write(`with-timeout: ${message}\n`);
73:   process.exit(2);

/**
 * A cached `vp` run executes each task in a clean environment: only a built-in set (`PATH`, `HOME`,
 * `CI`, ...) is forwarded, and anything else is invisible to the command *and* absent from the cache
 * fingerprint unless the task declares it in `env`. Measured, on a task declaring one variable:

 *     vp run --no-cache <task>   declared: yes   undeclared: yes

 * run, and the build still succeeds. This snapshot is the guard: it discovers every build-time env
 * read in the workspace and requires each one to be accounted for below, so adding a read without

1: // Installing the deployment's bundled output-format blueprints.
2: //
3: // The archives and their presentation come from a directory chosen at build time (see
4: // scripts/build-format-blueprints.mjs), so a deployment ships its own formats by pointing
5: // FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR at its own tree rather than by editing this repo.
6: //
7: // Installation writes an ordinary blueprint -- metadata into BLUEPRINTS, the code snapshot into
8: // BLUEPRINT_CONTENT -- exactly as publishing does. Nothing downstream knows these are special:
9: // no reserved id prefix, no fallback branch in the read path. Failure is tolerable: a deployment
10: // with none installed simply has no standard formats.
11: 
12: import { BlueprintMetadata, BlueprintPublicInfo } from "@gadgets/workshop-shared/api";
13: import { BlueprintKvRecord, parseBlueprintArchive } from "./blueprint-archive.js";
14: import { BundledFormatBlueprint, FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS } from "./generated/format-blueprints.js";
15: import { fingerprint } from "./admin-config.js";
16: import { createWorkshopLogger } from "./observability";
17: 
18: const logger = createWorkshopLogger("workshop.formats");
19: 
20: type InstallEnv = Pick<Cloudflare.Env, "BLUEPRINTS" | "BLUEPRINT_CONTENT">;
21: 
22: /**
23:  * Identifies the exact set of bundled blueprints a deployment has installed, and how. Compared
24:  * with what was installed last time, so any change here triggers reinstallation.
25:  *
26:  * Everything that ends up in the installed metadata contributes, not just `revision`: editing a
27:  * description would otherwise build, deploy, and change nothing on a deployment that had already
28:  * installed. `revision` covers the one input this can't see, the archive bytes.
29:  */
30: export function formatBlueprintsManifestVersion(): string {
31:   return FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS
32:       .map(e => `${e.blueprintId}@${e.revision}+` +
33:           fingerprint(JSON.stringify([e.title, e.description, e.author, e.output])))
34:       .toSorted()
35:       .join(",");
36: }

39: async function installOne(env: InstallEnv, entry: BundledFormatBlueprint)
40:     : Promise<BlueprintPublicInfo> {
41:   // Parse through the ordinary archive reader so a corrupt bundled file fails the same way an
42:   // uploaded one would, rather than producing a half-installed blueprint.
43:   let {metadata, contentLength, content} = await parseBlueprintArchive(
44:       new Response(Uint8Array.fromBase64(entry.archive) as BufferSource).body!);
45: 
46:   // R2 needs a known length, and the archive is already fully in memory (it came out of the
47:   // Worker bundle), so buffer rather than plumbing a FixedLengthStream through as the upload path
48:   // does for genuinely streamed uploads.
49:   let contentBytes = new Uint8Array(await new Response(content).arrayBuffer());
50:   if (contentBytes.byteLength !== contentLength) {
51:     throw new Error(`Archive declares ${contentLength} content bytes but holds ` +
52:         `${contentBytes.byteLength}.`);
53:   }

63:     output: entry.output,

1: // Spawn pnpm from a script without going through a shell.
2: //
3: // On Windows the `pnpm` on PATH is a `.cmd` shim. Node spawns processes directly rather than through
4: // a shell, so there is no extensionless `pnpm` to execute and the call fails with ENOENT. Naming the
5: // shim explicitly does not help either: since the fix for CVE-2024-27980 Node refuses to spawn
6: // `.cmd`/`.bat` without a shell and fails with EINVAL instead.
7: //
8: // `shell: true` makes the call work but is not safe here. A shell re-splits the command line, and
9: // the callers pass absolute paths built from the checkout location -- on a checkout whose path
10: // contains a space (`C:\Users\Some Name\...`) those arguments break apart.
11: //
12: // `npm_execpath` is the way out: under `pnpm run` it holds pnpm's own JS entry point, which `node`
13: // executes directly with no shell, so every argument keeps its exact value. Under `npm run` the same
14: // variable points at npm's CLI instead, so it is checked before being used -- substituting it
15: // unchecked would silently run `npm install` against a pnpm workspace.
16: 
17: // pnpm's JS entry, as `npm_execpath` spells it (`.cjs` or `.mjs` depending on how pnpm was
18: // installed). npm's `npm-cli.js` and the standalone `pnpm.exe`/`pnpm.cmd` shims do not match.
19: const PNPM_JS_ENTRY = /[\\/]pnpm\.[cm]?js$/i;
20: 
21: /**
22:  * `[command, args]` for running pnpm with `args`, to hand to `spawn`, `spawnSync` or `execFileSync`.
23:  *
24:  * Off Windows, and on Windows whenever the launcher was not pnpm, this is a plain `["pnpm", args]`:
25:  * an entry path this cannot support keeps today's loud ENOENT rather than quietly reaching for a
26:  * different package manager.
27:  *
28:  * `env` and `platform` are parameters only so the Windows branch stays testable on other platforms.
29:  */
30: export function pnpmCommand(
31:   args: string[],
32:   env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env,
33:   platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform,
34: ): [string, string[]] {
35:   const execPath = env.npm_execpath ?? "";
36:   return platform === "win32" && PNPM_JS_ENTRY.test(execPath)
37:     ? [process.execPath, [execPath, ...args]]
38:     : ["pnpm", args];
39: }
